https://taz.de/KI-Filme-in-China/!623043.title: KI-Filme in China: Angriff der Superintelligenz auf die Bilder
https://taz.de/KI-Filme-in-China/!623043.author: Tobias Kolonko
https://taz.de/KI-Filme-in-China/!623043.text:
KI-Filme in China: Angriff der Superintelligenz auf die Bilder
In chinesischen Kinos läuft derzeit ein komplett KI-erzeugter Science-Fiction-Film. Ein Flop – aber die Filmbranche ist durch die Entwicklung im rasanten Umbruch.
Das Filmplakat für „Sanxingdui: Future Past“ lockt: „Komm und blick in die Zukunft“. Der neue Science-Fiction-Film ist, samt Schauspielern und Ton, komplett von künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) erzeugt worden und läuft derzeit in den chinesischen Kinos. Doch die Zukunft scheint kaum jemanden zu interessieren. Die Säle bleiben so gut wie leer. Nach einem Monat spielte der 100 Minuten lange Film nur rund 250.000 Euro ein, ein Bruchteil der knapp 1,4 Millionen Euro, die er gekostet hat.
„Warum sollten Leute Geld bezahlen, um einen KI-Film zu sehen, wenn sie auf dem Handy jederzeit kostenlos KI-generierte Kurzvideos schauen können?“, sagt Yumeng, die im südchinesischen Zhuhai Film und Fernsehen studiert. Im Film reist eine Astronautin mehr als 3.000 Jahre in die Vergangenheit, in die Zeit der südwestchinesischen Sanxingdui-Zivilisation, um die Menschheit (ausgerechnet) vor einer KI-Superintelligenz zu retten. An manchen Stellen beeindrucken die futuristischen Szenen. An anderen erkennt man noch an den Gesichtsausdrücken und künstlich wirkenden Hintergründen, dass KI im Spiel war. Der Film enttäuscht aber mehr wegen des verwirrenden Drehbuchs als wegen der Qualität der künstlich generierten Bilder.
Im aktuellen KI-Wettrennen zwischen China und den USA liegt China klar vorn bei Text-zu-Video-Modellen, die aus kurzen Textbeschreibungen innerhalb von Sekunden Videos erzeugen können. Sora von OpenAI dagegen wurde im April wegen hoher Energiekosten und mangelnden Umsatzes eingestellt. Laut dem von der Stanford University erstellten AI Index 2026 sind acht der zehn besten Text-zu-Video-Modelle chinesisch.
Mikrodramen sind Fastfood fürs Handy
Ob auf den Werbebildschirmen der U-Bahn oder auf den Smartphones von Zugpassagieren und Taxifahrern: KI-Videos sind in China längst Teil des Alltags. Auch die äußerst beliebten Mikrodramen entstehen immer öfter mit KI. Allein im ersten Halbjahr waren es mehr als 210.000. Mikrodramen sind zumeist klischeehafte Miniserien mit ein- bis zweiminütigen Episoden, die oft im Hochkantformat gefilmt werden – Fastfood fürs Handy. Einige der KI-generierten Dramen haben Hunderte Millionen Aufrufe. Doch der Kinostart von „Sanxingdui: Future Past“ zeigt: KI-Videos sind nun nicht mehr auf Werbung und Handybildschirme beschränkt, sie drängen auch auf die große Leinwand.
„Chinesen sind KI gegenüber weniger skeptisch als Menschen im Westen“, sagt Fang, der letztes Jahr eine KI-Produktionsfirma gegründet hat. Aus dem Start-up ist inzwischen ein Betrieb mit acht Festangestellten geworden. Anfangs produzierte seine Firma nur Werbung, aber seit Neuestem arbeitet man auch an der Produktion von TV-Serien und Filmen. „Neue KI-Technologien werden in China extrem schnell übernommen“, sagt er. Das liege vor allem am enormen Wettbewerb der chinesischen Wirtschaft. Wer KI beherrscht, ist der Konkurrenz einen Schritt voraus. Das gilt besonders für junge Chinesen, bei denen die Arbeitslosigkeit seit Jahren über 15 Prozent liegt. Eltern setzen für die Zukunft ihrer Kinder vermehrt auf künstliche Intelligenz. Viele Ferienlager, in denen Jugendlichen KI-Kompetenzen beigebracht werden, waren diesen Sommer komplett ausgebucht.
Bevor er seine Firma gründete, arbeitete Fang hauptberuflich als Kameramann. Filme, die er gedreht hat, liefen bereits beim Locarno Film Festival und auf der Berlinale. Trotz dieser Erfolge fühlte er sich aber fast gezwungen, auf KI-Produktionen umzusteigen. „Schon vor dem KI-Boom war es schwer, als junger Kameramann genügend Geld zu verdienen“, sagt er. „Jetzt ist es noch viel schwieriger.“
Drei Minuten Kampfszene für weniger als 4.000 Euro
Am deutlichsten zeigen sich die Folgen der KI derzeit in der Mikrodrama-Branche, deren Umsatz seit einigen Jahren weit über dem des chinesischen Kinos liegt. Viele auf Mikrodramen spezialisierte Produktionshäuser stellen inzwischen komplett auf KI um. Zwar entstehen dadurch immer mehr Serien, doch Gehälter und Belegschaften schrumpfen. Besonders hart trifft es die Schauspieler. In Hengdian, einem der größten Filmstudios der Welt südlich von Hangzhou, drehten im vergangenen Jahr noch an jeder Ecke Filmcrews rund um die Uhr. Heute setzt das Studio auf Veranstaltungen und Tourismus, um die oft leeren Filmsets zu füllen.
Bei größeren kommerziellen Produktionen könnte sich ein ähnlicher Umschwung anbahnen. In chinesischen Medien erklärte der Regisseur der KI-generierten Serie „Beyond Wukong“, die seit August im Staatsfernsehen läuft, dass mit KI nur noch 100 Leute nötig seien, um die Arbeit von 2.000 zu erledigen. Eine dreiminütige Kampfszene koste statt einer halben Million Euro weniger als 4.000. Die durch KI verkleinerten Budgets gehen jetzt aber nicht mehr an Schauspieler, Tontechniker und Kostümdesigner, sondern größtenteils an milliardenschwere Tech-Konzerne. Vor allem ByteDance, der Mutterkonzern von Tiktok, profitiert. Dem Konzern gehört nicht nur die Mikrodrama-Plattform Hongguo, die inzwischen mehr tägliche Nutzer hat als Chinas drei größte klassische Streamingdienste zusammen, sondern auch das fortgeschrittenste Text-zu-Video-Modell Seedance.
Auch „Sanxingdui: Future Past“ wurde großteils mit Seedance produziert. Doch das Modell ist umstritten: Als ByteDance Anfang des Jahres eine neue Version veröffentlichte, überfluteten hyperrealistische KI-Videos soziale Medien, darunter auch viele Deepfakes von Prominenten wie Tom Cruise und Marvel-Superhelden. Große Hollywoodstudios warfen ByteDance vor, das Modell ohne Erlaubnis mit ihren Filmen trainiert zu haben. Disney und Paramount drohten sogar mit einer Klage, die bis jetzt jedoch ausblieb.
Für Studenten ist es schwer, in dieser rasanten Entwicklung Orientierung zu finden. „Die meisten meiner Kommilitonen machen jetzt ein Praktikum bei großen Tech-Firmen“, erzählt die Filmstudentin Yumeng. Auf WeChat kursiert ein Video von einer Jobmesse an der Pekinger Filmakademie, auf der vor allem KI-Firmen um Nachwuchs werben. Selbst etablierte Arthouse-Regisseure werden häufig von KI-Firmen angeworben, um deren Modelle weiterzuentwickeln. Auch die Hochschulen reagieren: Die Communication University of China, eine der führenden Medienhochschulen des Landes, hat 2025 mehrere künstlerische Studiengänge gestrichen und durch neue mit Schwerpunkt auf Technologie und KI ersetzt.
Für Yumeng kommt ein Praktikum bei einem KI-Unternehmen nicht infrage. Lieber würde sie nach dem Studium gar nicht erst in die Filmbranche einsteigen, als mit KI arbeiten zu müssen. Sie ist nicht die Einzige, die sich über KI-generierte Inhalte ärgert. Im Sommer sorgte für Aufruhr, dass die KI-Schauspielerin Fang Taozi aus einem berühmten Mikrodrama als Werbefigur den „Tragekomfort“ ihrer Kontaktlinsen pries. Als Gegenreaktion auf KI lässt sich auch der Überraschungserfolg des Low-Budget-Films „Niu Lai“ in China lesen. Der Film des Mutter-Sohn-Duos ist das Gegenteil von oberflächlich perfekten KI-Videos: Die Animation ist schlicht, die Figuren sind grob, die Dialoge holprig. Aber es sind genau diese Makel, die dem Film zu großer Beliebtheit verhalfen. In den Kinos spielte „Niu Lai“ etwa das 38-Fache von „Sanxingdui: Future Past“ ein.
Bedeutet der Flop von „Sanxingdui“, dass es so schnell keine KI-Filme mehr ins Kino schaffen? Regisseur Fang verneint das. „Das Ziel dieses Films war, vor allem zu zeigen, was mit KI schon möglich ist.“ In China sind weitere Filme angekündigt, auch in den USA steht im Dezember ein KI-Kinofilm an. Wie die Werke beim Publikum ankommen werden, ist noch unklar. Was klar ist: Die KI-Modelle werden immer besser.

Grâce à leur mobilisation, les 77 salariés de TK Accelis Plastic, filiale de Thyssenkrupp, sont parvenus à éviter leur vente au fonds de retournement Mutares. Ils se battent désormais pour des conditions de licenciement dignes.
Éviter de transformer le mauvais en pire. C’est le combat dans lequel se sont lancés les 77 salariés français de la société TK Accelis France, appartenant au géant allemand de la sidérurgie Thyssenkrupp.
Après des années de déficit, les salariés ont su en août que leur employeur se mettait en quête d’un repreneur et déployait un plan de sauvegarde de l’emploi (PSE) dans les six sites répartis sur le territoire, que compte cette branche. Un coup dur, mais le pire n’était pas encore arrivé.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.text:
Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming government
The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.
Delegations from Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Netanyahu’s Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday.
“The latest round of coalition talks… has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,” the two parties said in a joint statement.
“A follow-up meeting will be held,” they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details.
A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government, with the possibility of a 14‑day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.
His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra‑Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.
Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: Alcaraz puts Zverev in shade as world’s best beats No 1 for first ATP Finals title
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Tumaini Carayol
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
The titles of ATP world No 1 and the best male tennis player in the world are carried by two different names. This has always been clear throughout this messy, injury-ravaged men’s season but it was underlined in the grand finale as Carlos Alcaraz ended his campaign with a statement victory, defeating the top-ranked player, Alexander Zverev, 6-2, 7-6 (7) to win the ATP Finals for the first time.
So much of Alcaraz’s fortunes this season were defined by the wrist injury that forced him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer. No matter, he still managed to tick the two most important items off his to-do list this year.
After starting 2026 by becoming the youngest man in history to earn the career grand slam, he is now, at 23, the fourth man to win all four grand slams and the ATP Finals. Despite his long absence, he has missed only two of the four majors and two of the nine Masters 1000 events: the Canadian Open and Shanghai Masters.
Faster indoor courts were previously viewed as the conditions that make Alcaraz most vulnerable. It is fair to say that this is no longer true. Alcaraz ends his year on a 14-match winning streak after triumphing on two of the fastest courts, Paris and Turin.
This victory is all the more impressive considering he picked up a thigh injury during his match on Wednesday against Daniil Medvedev. Although he kept on winning, the Spaniard has been more cautious with his peerless movement and his leg has been heavily taped. He has learned that he does not always need to throw himself around the court at 100% intensity, that he can actually conserve energy, play more efficiently and still defeat the best players in the world. That might just be the most worrying development for the rest of the field.
Until the final, Zverev’s tournament had served as another demonstration of his enormous yet freakishly consistent serve, with the German not dropping serve at all en oute to the final. However, the opening game immediately underscored how much better Alcaraz is than the rest of the top 10.
The Spaniard immediately generated three break points on Zverev’s serve. In Zverev’s second service game, Alcaraz landed ample returns, forced Zverev into baseline exchanges and broke to love.
For much of the match, Alcaraz completely outplayed Zverev from the baseline. His concerns surrounding his thigh problems have forced him to play even more offensively as usual, and he has struck the ball so sweetly for most of the tournament, but he was also incredibly smart. He peppered Zverev with ample slices and slower balls, drawing short balls from the German by arresting his rhythm, before unleashing in full. Alcaraz’s forehand, the best in the world, usually commands all the attention, but he struck his backhand incredibly well all match.
However, even for a player who has won so much at such a young age, he rarely makes things easy for himself. From 6-2, 4-2, Alcaraz began to spray unforced errors as he fell to 4-5, 0-30 on his serve in set two. Then, after recovering to lead 3-0 in the tie‑break, Alcaraz suddenly trailed by triple set point at 3-6.
During this stretch, Zverev served well, he forced the Spaniard to earn every point through his consistent defence and came up with improvisational solutions to Alcaraz’s drop shots and variation on some decisive moments. The Spaniard, however, was extremely poor.
Things may not often be straightforward for Alcaraz: his ability to play his best tennis when it most matters remains an astounding quality. To the surprise of nobody at all, he locked in, saved the three set points, earned a match point with a sickly sweet point-ending drop shot and then, without hesitation, he pounded a backhand down-the-line winner to close out the victory.
After ample discourse surrounding his credibility as the new No 1, which Zverev complained about during the Paris Masters, he did respond in the right way on the court here, reaching the final with wins against four top 10 opponents.
But there are levels to this game and the gap between Alcaraz and the rest of the field in Turin this year is vast. He ends his individual season by providing an unforgettable reminder of the excellence the sport had to go without for so long.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Five key takeaways for Pochettino
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Five key takeaways for Pochettino
United suffer their worst result under a new manager in 100 years as Liverpool cruise past Mauricio Pochettino’s side.
If Mauricio Pochettino had any doubt about the size of the job in front of him at Manchester United, his players confirmed his worst fears within 13 minutes of his first game in charge – a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.
As the home side surged into a two-goal lead in the opening exchanges at Anfield, with the away side reduced to 10 men, the sinking sensation for United – who are second bottom of the Premier League – immediately returned.
Any ‘new-manager bounce’, as feared by Reds manager Andoni Iraola, had no time to materialise with a rash challenge from Lenny Yoro on Alexander Isak leading to a straight red in the eighth minute.
The resulting free-kick was powered home by Dominik Szoboszlai, with Florian Wirtz thereafter converting a sharp attack in a flash – ending the match as a contest.
Pochettino slammed the decision to send off Yoro after the game, but there was a familiar feeling about the performance overall.
Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at five key takeaways as the opening salvo of the ninth manager since United’s last league title in 2013 fell apart – resulting in the worst start for a new manager of the club in 100 years.
Was the referee right to send off Manchester United’s Lenny Yoro?
Even though United have greater concerns, the answer was undoubtedly: no. The question for the referee, in sending off Yoro for denying a goalscoring opportunity, had four considerations: distance between the offence and the goal, general direction of the play, likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball, and location and number of defenders.
Of those guidelines, the most pertinent were the direction of play, which was at an angle across the box, and the likelihood of keeping control of the ball – Isak arguably had no control of it at all after a heavy first touch that allowed United keeper Senne Lammens to gather.
VAR (video assistant referee) had the chance to ask the referee to reconsider his decision, but decided there was no clear and obvious error. Had the referee reviewed the red card, then he would have surely decided a yellow card would have sufficed.
The play that led to the card being shown, however, was even more questionable than the outcome.
Was Pochettino right to bench Maguire for Man United?
The release of the team sheets, an hour and 15 minutes before kickoff, was the first moment all United fans looked to.
For all the pre-game comments by Pochettino, the Argentinean’s starting 11 was always going to be the first true sense of his evaluation of United’s current woes.
Dropping defender Harry Maguire, a former club captain, was a massive call – all the more so given the inexperience of Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt, who were both selected ahead of the ex-England stalwart.
The ref’s mistake in sending off Yoro was clear, but Yoro and de Ligt were heavily exposed in the play that led to the sending-off.
The latter is easing his way back into first-team action after a year out with a back injury and found himself in no-man’s land as Isak chased a long ball. Yoro sought to cover, but was clumsy and ill-advised in his attempt, allowing Isak to draw what was only a soft challenge and connection.
United were plucky after the change forced by the sending-off, with Maguire replacing the clearly, and understandably, disappointed Bryan Mbeumo.
Maguire’s fine, last-ditch block from Isak’s close-range pivot and shot saved United’s blushes five minutes before the break, and made Pochettino’s first big call look all the worse.
A scuffed attempt at a clearance early in the second half by de Ligt allowed Isak clean through only for the Liverpool forward to slice his effort.
By the time Rio Ngumoha added a 66th-minute third, all the questions about a defence that had previously shipped 30 goals in 15 games this season had been answered. The fourth from Victor Munoz was inevitable, and it could have been a lot worse for United on the day.
Their last defeat at Anfield was a 7-0 victory for the home side – a repeat was certainly possible had Liverpool been more clinical.
Matters were so bad that the former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher commented on Sky Sports that he “felt sorry” for de Ligt prior to his eventual substitution in the second half.
The consensus was that Pochettino made the wrong call before the start.
What other Man United changes did Pochettino make at Liverpool?
Yoro and de Ligt have been peripheral figures in their time with the Old Trafford club, for varying reasons including injury, but they were not the only big calls made by Pochettino.
Another injury-plagued player, Patrick Dorgu, was also given a start – and in a formation which was not wholly clear. The popular Amad Diallo was forced to make do with a place on the bench alongside Maguire.
Dorgu, whose form has been indifferent at best, can operate as a wide defender or attacker. It appeared as though he was given some licence on the left to get forward, with United reverting to a back four, Lisandro Martinez covering on the flank in defence and Diogo Dalot holding back on the right.
Whether it was a back four or five to begin with – the latter explaining the absence of the more forward-minded Diallo – United were quickly forced to a five with the sending-off and the sacrifice of Mbeumo at the other end of the pitch.
Not only was the decision to pick two less experienced centre-backs at Anfield a monumental – and ultimately costly – call, the move to switch to an unfamiliar feel across the backline was a painful lesson for Pochettino, who himself is more accustomed to a 4-2-3-1 setup.
What next for Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino?
With 19th-placed United mired in the Premier League drop zone, the UEFA Champions League appears a sideshow, but a trip to Sporting Lisbon awaits on Wednesday.
In some ways, Europe’s elite club competition, which United have returned to after a three-year absence, may well give Pochettino a free hit to explore how he can get the best out of a beleaguered group.
The absolute priority for the Red Devils has to be channelling their efforts towards climbing the domestic ladder and pulling well away from an unthinkable relegation scrap.
Yoro will be available for the match in the Portuguese capital, which means Pochettino must wrestle with his decision to pick the young duo in defence. Failing to pick both Yoro and de Ligt at Sporting would almost appear an early admission of error.
What is the wider context for Manchester United and Pochettino?
Former United captain Roy Keane was at Anfield as a pundit for Sky Sports and, in his analysis of the overall display, described his old club’s performance at Anfield as “desperate”.
Harsh words for the current playing group are nothing new. Their latest low leaves them with the worst defensive record in top-flight football in Europe.
Pochettino at least has time on his side to reverse United’s worst league start in 40 years, but some short-term solutions will be expected by the time Brentford arrive at Old Trafford next Saturday.
Should Pochettino not find some considerable longer-term strategies soon, then the desperate may well turn to the unimaginable.
The heat is turning up for the Red Devils, and the patience of the fans has already run thin with the players this season.
The much-maligned ownership of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos group can also expect prolonged protests, as seen of late.
Change in the dugout appears as though it will not be anywhere near enough to reverse a trend 13 years in the making – and the fans’ unswerving support of Pochettino’s predecessor, Michael Carrick, attests to the fact that wholesale reformation is warranted.

https://taz.de/EU-und-Grossbritannien-na.text:
EU-Forderungen an Großbritannien : Kleingeist statt strategisches Denken
Die EU macht ihr neues Abkommen mit Großbritannien von Vorzugsbehandlung bei britischen Studiengebühren abhängig. Sie verkennt die Zeichen der Zeit.
I n der Welt von 2026 wäre der Brexit von 2016 nicht passiert. Europa muss zusammenstehen, um in der Welt zu bestehen, das wissen heute alle. Was die Verteidigung der Ukraine angeht, spielt es keine Rolle, ob Großbritannien Teil der EU ist oder nicht. Vorläufig jedoch wird das neue weitreichende Abkommen, das London und Brüssel geschlossen haben, blockiert – weil die EU verlangt, dass britische Universitäten Studierende aus EU-Staaten von den für Ausländer geltenden Studiengebühren ausnehmen.
Die britische Regierung hat dafür jetzt sechs Monate Zeit, sonst tritt alles andere nicht in Kraft. Dabei besteht „alles andere“ auch schon vor allem aus britischen Zugeständnissen, nämlich der Selbstverpflichtung, in einigen Wirtschaftsbereichen EU-Regeln automatisch komplett zu übernehmen. Das Junktim mit Studiengebühren ist ein verheerendes Zeichen. Viele „Eurokraten“ schicken ihre Kinder gerne auf britische Spitzenuniversitäten, weil es in der EU keine Spitzenuniversitäten gibt.
Sie verlangen nun Vergünstigungen. Eine kleine Zahl bildungsprivilegierter Europäer soll es besser haben als Afrikaner, Asiaten und Amerikaner. Mit welchem Recht? Und wer kommt auf die absurde Idee, dass das wichtiger ist als die strategische Einheit Europas? Nichts hindert die EU daran, selbst die Förderung für die Studenten auf der Insel lockerzumachen.
taz debatte
Die taz ist eine unabhängige, linke und meinungsstarke Tageszeitung. In unseren Kommentaren, Essays und Debattentexten streiten wir seit der Gründung der taz im Jahr 1979. Oft können und wollen wir uns nicht auf eine Meinung einigen. Deshalb finden sich hier teils komplett gegenläufige Positionen – allesamt Teil des sehr breiten linken Meinungsspektrums.
Aber nein, die britischen Universitäten sollen auf Einnahmen verzichten, im Namen Europas. Die britische Regierung könnte im Gegenzug die Milliardensummen einfordern, die ehemalige EU-Studenten noch an offenen Studienkrediten aus der Zeit vor dem Brexit schulden. Doch Andy Burnham traut sich nicht, seinen „Reset“ mit Europa zu dem schmutzigen Geschäft zu machen, wie es die EU gerade praktiziert.
In der EU wird mit zweierlei Maß gemessen. So verlangt in Brüssel niemand von Kanada die Übernahme von EU-Recht oder günstigere Studiengebühren für Europäer. Bei Großbritannien fällt die EU in den krämerischen Kleingeist von vor zehn Jahren zurück.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Eric Berger
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy”.
The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was put at risk by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.
Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s CEO on 12 November after allegations surfaced of extramarital relationships with the suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees.
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, had been executive director of Megaspeed International. Megaspeed facilitated about $12bn in chip sales, in violation of export controls in the US, where the Trump administration has prohibited the selling of advanced AI chips to China.
On Sunday’s edition of CNN’s State of the Union, the Trump administration’s national intelligence director, Jay Clayton, said he suspected China was able to obtain Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips.
He also said on Fox News Sunday: “There are chips that have ended up in places that they should not.”
Kennedy said he was “less interested in … what [Huang] did” than in asking the Trump administration’s commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, and its treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, about how China was evidently able to circumvent US “export controls”.
“Mr Huang … did what he did. I hope he had a good time. It was the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy,” Kennedy said.
Lutnick has faced scrutiny over allegedly ignoring warnings that Megaspeed was smuggling chips to China. Other administration leaders, including Bessent, wanted to put Megaspeed on a trade blacklist – but the commerce department stalled enforcement of it.
Kennedy said he could only conclude commerce department leaders are either “so incompetent you wouldn’t put them in charge of a food truck” – or “they knowingly allowed this to happen”.
He said he wanted to get Bessent and Lutnick under oath in front of a Senate committee to “answer some hard questions”.
“And if secretary Lutnick is giving our chips away, he needs to stop it, in my opinion,” Kennedy said.
Bessent said on Sunday’s edition of CBS News’s Face the Nation that the Trump administration had been in touch with Nvidia’s temporary management, lead directors and lawyers while trying to find out who was in charge of compliance at the company.
“It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was,” Bessent said on the program.
Kennedy, a former Louisiana state treasurer who began his political career as a Democrat before switching parties and becoming a staunch Trump administration ally, delivers many of the colloquialisms that have become his calling card with a southern US drawl.
Many believe Kennedy resorts to the drawl to come off as folksy – while he holds degrees from Vanderbilt University, the University of Virginia School of Law and the UK’s Oxford University, and is estimated to be one of the wealthiest US senators.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.text:
Bahrain says Iranian strike wounds two, one critically
Bahrain said on Sunday that two people were wounded in an Iranian strike the previous day on “a civilian industrial site” in the Gulf kingdom, which has faced several attacks this week.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has repeatedly said they targeted US facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed earlier in November.
"In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain… a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded," Bahrain's interior ministry said on X.
"His condition is stable. A Pakistani resident was also wounded and is in critical condition."
Residents had seen smoke rising above Sitra Island, east of Manama, which hosts several industrial facilities, including a refinery operated by the state-owned oil company Bapco, AFP reported.
In a statement carried by Iranian state media on Saturday evening, the IRGC said they had attacked US Patriot air defence systems with missiles and drones at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, in response to the “continued violations of the airspace” of the Islamic Republic.
Bahrain's foreign ministry dismissed the IRGC's account, saying the site hit was purely civilian and industrial, calling the attack a direct danger to civilians and a violation of the kingdom's sovereignty.
Bahrain's neighbour Saudi Arabia on Sunday also condemned Tehran for its attacks on Gulf countries.
The Saudi foreign ministry expressed on X "the strongest condemnation and denunciation... of the criminal Iranian attacks against a civilian industrial facility in the brotherly Kingdom of Bahrain".
As a result of the heinous Iranian attacks on Bahrain yesterday, a Bahraini citizen with disabilities sustained injuries and is in stable condition, while a Pakistani resident was also injured and is in critical condition. Both are receiving treatment in the hospital. #Bahrain #MOI

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Democrats capture at least 258 House seats in largest sweep since 1992
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Associated Press
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
House Democrats have secured their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in a midterm election sweep unseen since 1992 that creates not only vast opportunities to govern but also intense pressure to deliver on campaign promises and priorities.
Democrats have gained 44 House seats so far, four more than the 40 they picked up in Donald Trump’s first midterm in 2018.
The 258-seat tally was reached on Sunday, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina. Four other House races remain outstanding: one each in Minnesota and Tennessee, and two in Louisiana that are heading to a December runoff.
Republicans will have at least 173 seats in the minority.
The milestone in the 435-member House sets up a divided government, with the Senate also in Democratic hands and with a Republican president in the White House. Emboldened Democrats are preparing a 100-day agenda to address high costs of living while also confronting Trump with a vast oversight agenda for the remainder of his second term in office.
The Democrats’ majority will be bigger than any the party has seen in elections since Bill Clinton was first elected president in 1992 (258) or the election of Barack Obama in 2008 (257), yet not quite the high-water mark of the Franklin D Roosevelt-era, which saw House Democratic majorities swell past 300.
It presents opportunities and challenges ahead.
“Like, hell yeah, we should feel pressure,” said Democratic representative Jason Crow of Colorado, a former army ranger.
“There are people dying in this country and people losing their healthcare, losing their livelihoods, losing their farms, being terrorized from ICE,” he said at the Capitol, referring to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. “If you don’t feel a sense of urgency and pressure in this job, and a desperation to deliver for folks, then you don’t belong under this Capitol dome.”
The numbers underscore the extraordinary scale of Democratic wins, which spanned from the strongest Republican states to the midwest and east coast as voters, angry over high prices and the Iran war and concerned over corruption, made clear their discontent with Trump.
Taking control of both the House and the Senate come January, the Democrats will carry with them the backing of voters and the expectations to deliver. The Senate Democrats won a 56-seat majority in the 100-member chamber, their biggest advantage in over a decade.
The Democrats, as part of their 100-day agenda, are planning swift votes to reverse the Republicans’ Medicaid cuts and restore the Affordable Care Act tax credits the Republicans allowed to expire.
Democrats have vowed to marshal their subpoena powers and launch a flurry of investigations to exert the role of Congress as a check on presidential power. That includes plans to probe how Trump and his family have become wealthier since he returned to office. Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, who is in line to become House speaker, has not ruled out trying to impeach Trump for a third time.
“This is a historic moment for our country. This is one of the largest classes we have seen,” said Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, the progressive New York congresswoman, at the Capitol.
She called the big numbers “a mandate for change”.
Representative Tom Suozzi, a centrist Democrat from New York and an accountant by profession, said the House Democrats should focus 75% of their time on affordability issues and 25% on accountability.
“Everything should be tied back to the people – and how it’s affecting the people,” he said.
For example, he said, as the Democrats launch investigations into Trump’s financial dealings, they should be connecting the dots: “How does that affect people’s pocketbooks?”
After the Republican House speaker Mike Johnson struggled to keep the House functioning for the past two years with a narrow 218-214 Republican majority – meaning any few GOP lawmakers could derail the agenda – the Democrats wide margin provides the new leadership much more room to maneuver.
Jeffries, who is poised to make history as the first Black speaker of the House if his colleagues elect him to the job on 3 January 2027, will be able to lose dozens of Democrats on any given vote and still have the 218 needed for passage.
Republicans saw their number of House seats fall to one of the lowest tallies in decades. Representative Jim Jordan of Ohio, who was elected by his colleagues to be the Republican leader in the minority, vowed to fight their way back to power.
“Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families,” Jordan said.

https://taz.de/Regierungsgespraeche-in-I.title: Regierungsgespräche in Israel: Kein Partner für die Koalition
https://taz.de/Regierungsgespraeche-in-I.author: Susanne Knaul
https://taz.de/Regierungsgespraeche-in-I.text:
Regierungsgespräche in Israel : Kein Partner für die Koalition
Dass Israels Oppositionschef mit Netanjahus Partei Koalitionsgespräche führen will, überrascht. War doch sein erklärtes Ziel, diesen zu Fall zu bringen.
A usgerechnet mit dem Likud von Benjamin Netanjahu will Gadi Eisenkot nun Koalitionsgespräche führen. Der Chef des Anti-Netanjahu-Lagers musste – wie alle Fraktionen – auch Vertreter der Partei des noch amtierenden Regierungschefs einladen. Aber gleich „Marathonverhandlungen“, wie er es nennt? Eine Koalition zu erwägen mit Netanjahu oder auch nur Teilen der Partei, die ihn über Jahre an der Macht gehalten hat, ist nichts anderes als Verrat an den WählerInnen.
Ein Blick auf Netanjahus zehn Bedingungen für eine große Koalition reicht, um zu wissen, dass eine Einigung ohnehin illusorisch ist. Niemand außer ihm selbst soll demnach in den kommenden vier Jahren Ministerpräsident sein. Zudem dürfe es keine staatliche Untersuchungskommission zu eventuellem Fehlverhalten von Regierung und Sicherheitsapparat vor, während und nach dem Hamas-Massaker vom 7. Oktober 2023 geben. Genau das steht allerdings ganz oben auf der Agenda, die Eisenkot umsetzen will, wenn er erst einmal den Regierungsposten übernommen hat.
Vollkommen absurd ist zudem Netanjahus Bedingung, seine bisherigen rassistischen Partner Itamar Ben-Gvir und Bezalel Smotrich in die noch zu gründende nationale Einheitsregierung mitzunehmen.
Nahost-Debatten
Der Israel-Palästina-Konflikt wird vor allem in linken Kreisen kontrovers diskutiert. Auch in der taz existieren dazu teils grundverschiedene Positionen. In diesem Schwerpunkt finden Sie alle Kommentare und Debattenbeiträge zum Thema „Nahost“.
Nichts davon passt mit dem zusammen, was Eisenkot seinen WählerInnen versprochen hat. So liegt die Vermutung nah, dass es sich bei den „Marathonverhandlungen“ um ein Manöver handelt. Die Frage ist nur, worauf der Chef der Partei mit dem Namen „Jaschar“, was so was wie „Aufrichtigkeit“ bedeutet, damit abzielt.
Für aufrechte DemokratInnen stünde jetzt die Suche nach Parteien an, mit denen man politische Inhalte teilt: die Vereinte Liste der arabischen Fraktionen zum Beispiel. Die hätte bestimmt nichts gegen eine Untersuchungskommission zum 7. Oktober einzuwenden und auch nicht gegen eine erneute Betrachtung der Justizreform. Dass Eisenkot trotzdem ein Zusammengehen mit den arabischen PolitikerInnen ablehnt, zeigt leider, dass er in Sachen Rassismus Netanjahu nicht sehr weit nachsteht.
Gemeinsam für freie Presse
Die taz gehört zu 100 Prozent ihren Leser:innen und ist damit nicht nur konzernfrei, sondern auch kostenfrei zugänglich. Alle Artikel stellen wir frei zur Verfügung, ohne Paywall. Gerade in diesen Zeiten müssen Einordnungen und Informationen allen zugänglich sein. Unsere Leser:innen müssen nichts bezahlen, wissen aber, dass kritischer, unabhängiger Journalismus nicht aus dem Nichts entsteht. Dafür sind wir sehr dankbar. Damit wir auch morgen noch unseren Journalismus machen können, brauchen wir mehr Unterstützung für taz zahl ich. Dank Ihnen haben wir nun die 50.000 erreicht. So viele unterstützen freiwillig und regelmäßig. Noch nicht dabei? Werden Sie jetzt Teil der Community! Jetzt unterstützen

https://www.humanite.fr/en-debat/budget/.title: Macron veut inscrire la règle d’or sur les déficits publics dans la Constitution : le chant du cygne jupitérien
https://www.humanite.fr/en-debat/budget/.author: Aurélien Soucheyre
https://www.humanite.fr/en-debat/budget/.text:
Macron veut inscrire la règle d’or sur les déficits publics dans la Constitution : le chant du cygne jupitérien
Voilà qu’Emmanuel Macron rêve d’inscrire une nouvelle ligne à sa gloire sur sa page Wikipédia. Quoi de plus beau, juste avant de partir, qu’une réforme constitutionnelle ? D’après la Tribune dimanche, le président souhaite convoquer le Congrès en janvier, afin d’inscrire la règle d’or sur les déficits publics dans notre loi fondamentale.
Pareille entreprise est des plus délicates, surtout pour un chef d’État démonétisé, impopulaire et interdit de se représenter en 2027. Sauf que l’Élysée entend exhumer un texte vieux de 2011, déjà voté dans les mêmes termes par l’Assemblée et le Sénat à la fin du mandat de Nicolas Sarkozy. L’occasion est trop belle.
Il n’y a plus qu’à obtenir les trois cinquièmes des votes des députés et des sénateurs réunis à Versailles et l’affaire sera dans le sac. Le tout sans débat public dans le pays, et sans aucune possibilité d’amendement par les parlementaires actuels. Soit du pur opportunisme technique, l’une des armes préférées de Macron.
La proposition, présente dans les très austéritaires programmes de Gabriel Attal, Édouard Philippe, Bruno Retailleau et Marine Le Pen, vise à ce que la France ne puisse plus dépenser plus qu’elle ne gagne lors des votes de ses budgets (celui de l’État comme celui de la Sécurité sociale).
Il est assez cocasse de voir que le président qui n’a pas proposé un seul exercice à l’équilibre en dix ans, creusant la dette comme jamais, offrant des centaines et des centaines de milliards de cadeaux aux plus riches et aux entreprises sans même en faire le calcul, vient donner des leçons de tenue de comptes en partant.
Le tout, alors que l’Allemagne a assoupli sa règle d’or, afin de pouvoir financer sa défense et la transition climatique. C’est qu’un emprunt n’est pas mauvais en lui-même. Tout dépend sur quoi il s’appuie et ce qu’il soutient : les marchés financiers et les milliardaires, ou l’épargne populaire et un gigantesque effort pour l’écologie, l’industrie et la justice sociale ?
Là n’est pas vraiment la question pour Macron. Jupiter veut affirmer qu’il a encore la main. Quitte à reprendre une demande de Jordan Bardella, qui lui a soufflé l’idée. Le 5 novembre, le président du RN l’invitait à instaurer une règle d’or, « dans un ultime geste salutaire pour le pays ». Quoi de plus beau, en effet, et de plus cohérent, que de finir le quinquennat en donnant le point à l’extrême droite ?
Le média que les milliardaires ne peuvent pas s’acheter
Nous ne sommes financés par aucun milliardaire. Et nous en sommes fiers ! Mais nous sommes confrontés à des défis financiers constants. Soutenez-nous ! Votre don sera défiscalisé : donner 5€ vous reviendra à 1.65€. Le prix d’un café.
Je veux en savoir plus !

Iran unveils new launcher that can fire two missiles at once
Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher, as senior military commanders touted the Islamic Republic's capabilities in defiant messages to the United States.
"A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time," Iranian state television reported on Saturday.
State television broadcast footage of Ahmad Vahidi, commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and Majid Mousavi, head of the IRGC's Aerospace Force, touring an underground missile base.
The two commanders were shown riding on top of a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment.
"The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation," Vahidi said.
"Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy," said Mousavi.
During the US-Israeli war on Iran, strikes targeted the country's missile capabilities and hit its nuclear sites for a second time, though the extent of the damage remains unclear.
Earlier this month, the IRGC unveiled what it described as new underground "missile cities" housing ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as launchers.

https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.title: I covered myself in sleep trackers to find the very best
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.author: Christine Persaud
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.text:
Getting quality sleep is just as crucial as getting enough sleep. And how you feel in the morning only tells part of the story. Smartwatches, smart bands, smart rings and sleep earbuds can all help fill in the details: how long it took you to doze off, how long you spent in deep sleep, how restless you were, your resting heart rate, even if you have night-time breathing difficulties.
Armed with this information, you can learn how your lifestyle affects your sleep. Maybe your after dinner cappuccino triggers a night of tossing and turning, or you’re more restful after evening workouts. As the wise GI Joe once said, knowing is half the battle. And the more you know about your sleep, the better chance you have of improving it.
Why you should trust me
As a consumer technology journalist for more than two decades, I began wearing fitness trackers in the early 2010s and have since reviewed hundreds of products in the sleep and fitness space. After spending more than 15 years tracking my sleep nightly, I have a deep understanding of how wearables work, which brands and products are reliable and how to best interpret app data.
How I tested
I wore up to five wearables at a time (two wrist devices, two rings, and earbuds) for at least seven nights each. Every morning, I plotted sleep data into a spreadsheet, including duration, sleep stages (light, REM, deep, awake), along with average sleep heart rate and heart rate variability (HRV) when available.
The Oura Ring 5 served as our benchmark for accuracy, since it is widely considered to be among the most accurate consumer wearables for sleep tracking. A study by the Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute (MDPI), for example, found Oura Ring’s data to be virtually identical to a polysomnogram (PSG) for all sleep stage measurements – that’s the gold standard method they use in sleep labs.
I also evaluated each tracker for design (is it comfortable to wear, especially overnight?), battery life (do I have to charge it frequently?), and the companion app (is it confusing or easy to read?).
Overall, I tested 11 wearables, some of which I spent significant time with before while reviewing them individually. Other wearables I have recently evaluated that I am confident would not make the cut or that have been replaced by newer models are listed as well.
I keep certain products on hand for future comparative reviews. Some products were sent specifically for consideration in this piece and were returned to the manufacturer if requested, except earbuds for hygienic reasons.
Best overall sleep tracker: 
Oura Ring 5
Not only is the Oura Ring 5 the sleekest and slimmest smart ring out there, it’s also the most accurate and easiest to live with.
Why we love it: Part gadget, part fashion accessory, the Oura Ring 5 comes in six color options, from traditional black to elegant Deep Rose. The barely-there design is so minimalist you’ll forget you’re even wearing it, yet it accurately captures detailed sleep data, including efficiency, restfulness, latency and timing.
Easy-to-read bar graphs in the app let you know what areas need improvement. Had restless sleep? Maybe you need to refrain from consuming liquids before bed to avoid nightly trips to the bathroom. Do you take too long to fall asleep? Look into softer lighting, cooler temperatures, white noise or less screen time right before bed. I love the “sleep debt” figure that continuously calculates the discrepancy between how much sleep you got v how much you need. It motivated me to make better decisions to close the gap.
If the info from the app isn’t enough, the Oura Advisor AI assistant is like having your own personal (virtual) sleep coach. Ask it questions about your sleep, such as how to improve, or even ideas for a good before-bed snack.
It’s a shame that … You need a $6 monthly subscription to benefit from all the great features of Oura Ring 5. And even though the battery lasts for about six to nine days, some competitors last longer. Plus, it only comes with a wired charging dock – you need to buy the wireless charging case separately.
Sizes: 6-13
Finish options: Silver, Brushed Silver, Gold, Deep Rose, Black, Stealth
Material: Full titanium
Battery life: Six to nine days
Subscription: Required for all meaningful data, $6 monthly or $70 annually
Best budget:
Fitbit Air
This incredibly thin wristband is inexpensive and free of distractions, but also impressively accurate.
Why we love it: With no screen, the Fitbit Air doesn’t bombard you with notifications and data; it just works passively in the background. When you want to know more – about sleep, steps, heart rate – open the app, sync and explore. The sensors sit on the inside of a thin strap that is incredibly comfortable to wear all day and overnight. It comes in fabric or metal mesh, but Google also offers a silicone accessory band.
The Fitbit Air’s data matched the data from our benchmark Oura Ring 5, closer than any of the other device I tested. This includes total sleep, deep sleep, HRV and near-identical heart rate readings throughout the testing period. The only big discrepancy came from awake time, where it deviated from the Oura by about 40 minutes on average. For example, one night, the Oura Ring 5 logged 58 minutes of awake time, while Fitbit Air only counted 16 awake minutes.
It’s a shame that … You need a $10 monthly subscription to Google Health Premium to unlock detailed sleep analysis and an AI coach, but it does provide enough value to justify it. Battery life of seven days is decent, but it’s not as good as other screenless models.
Sizes: One size (130-210mm wrist size for textile/polyurethane), 130-175 or 165-210 mm (silicone)
Finish options: Obsidian, Berry, Lavender, Fog
Material: Recycled polycarbonate and PBT plastics, silicone
Battery life: Up to seven days
Subscription: Google Health Premium, $10 monthly or $100 annually (optional)
Best for iPhone users: 
Apple Watch Series 12
The Apple Watch may be best known for flashy apps, fitness tracking and endlessly customizable bands, but it also makes a great sleep tracker.
Why we love it: The newest Apple Watch looks similar to the last few generations, but it now comes in ceramic, titanium or scratch-resistant aluminum, along with new finishes, including the lovely Dark Bronze of my review sample. I found it comfortable to wear overnight, and the data is easy to read from the watch face and the Health app.
After many years of wearing different Apple Watch models, I have noticed they often overstate deep sleep and understate awake time. This remains true for the newest model, but it comes pretty close to the Oura in tracking other sleep data, with the smallest differential for sleep duration, stages, sleep heart rate and HRV. It also had the closest REM readings to Oura of any device.
Beneath the basic stats, you can also dive deeper and compare your average sleep for the year to date with the year prior, providing value for longtime Apple Watch wearers. Like only a few peers, the Apple Watch can detect the breathing anomalies that align with sleep apnea. It’s not an official test – but it provides enough info to help you decide whether to consult a medical professional.
Besides tracking sleep, the Apple Watch is also a perfect iPhone companion for notifications, fitness tracking, Siri AI voice assistance, and with Apple’s new Health Sensing System, accurate heart-rate tracking.
It’s a shame that … The battery only lasts 24 hours per charge. You also need an iPhone, so Android owners are out of luck.
Sizes: 42mm, 46mm
Finish options: Dark Bronze, Light Gold, Black, Space Grey (aluminum), Radiant Gold, Natural (titanium), Pearl White, Night Blue (ceramic)
Material: Aluminum, titanium, ceramic
Battery life: Up to 24 hours (38 hours in Low Power Mode)
Subscription: None
Best for Android users: 
Google Pixel Watch 5
One of the most beautiful Android smartwatches you can buy is also an excellent tool to collect accurate sleep data and get AI-based guidance for adopting better sleep habits.
Why we love it: This comfortable-to-wear smartwatch for Android owners does a fairly good job of calculating sleep and stages, and especially HRV. You can also see how various factors such as restlessness and time-to-sleep compare with the typical range for people of your same age and gender. Its biggest weakness is inconsistent REM times, which were sometimes way above or way below, and other times spot on.
You need a Google Health Premium subscription ($10 monthly) to unlock sleep breathing trends, and AI Coach to ask questions about your sleep. But you get most of the core sleep metrics for free, including sleep duration, stages, score, restlessness, heart rate, and breathing quality. Since you can log meals, stress, alcohol or caffeine consumption and more, AI Coach can pick up on potential triggers for poor sleep, like having coffee too close to bedtime, and bring them to your attention.
Like the Apple Watch, the Pixel Watch 5 puts all sorts of other features on your wrist, from notifications to controlling smart home devices, and even answering questions via Gemini voice assistance. If you want those bells and whistles, it’s worth getting.
It’s a shame that … It isn’t a huge step up from the Pixel Watch 4. The 40-hour battery life means you need to charge it every day and a half. And you need a Google Health Premium subscription to unlock deeper sleep analysis. It also does not natively work with the iPhone.
Sizes: 41mm, 45mm
Finish options: Matte Black, Polished Silver, Satin Pyrite, Champagne Gold
Material: Aluminum
Battery life: Up to 30 hours, 48 hours in Battery Saver mode (41mm), up to 40 hours, 72 hours in Battery Saver Mode (46mm)
Subscription: Google Health Premium, $10 monthly or $100 annually (optional)
Best for no subscription: 
Garmin Cirqa
If you hate the idea of paying a monthly fee, the Garmin Cirqa works great without a subscription and also excels at tracking workouts.
Why we love it: The Cirqa offers accurate sleep tracking, activity tracking and vitals for one low price of entry. Garmin does technically offer a subscription service called Connect+, but it’s not worth it for most people and doesn’t offer any advancements in sleep tracking.
While thicker and wider than others, wearing the Garmin Cirqa is still comfortable. The battery lasts up to 10 days, and the two band sizes can accommodate wrists of any size.
As for accuracy, this band tracked closely with the Oura on light sleep, and fairly close on deep sleep, REM and HRV. Like the Fitbit Air, awake times are its biggest weakness, as it consistently recorded significantly less awake time.
Along with providing data incuding average SpO2 (blood oxygen saturation) while sleeping and number of restless moments, the Cirqa provides sleep guidance in the app. It might say you need more sleep after a short night, for example, and nudge you to get to bed at a specific time tonight to make up for it.
It also tracks whether the midpoint of your sleep was behind, ahead of or at your usual internal rhythm. This helps determine your circadian rhythm, and whether you’re a morning person or a night person. It can help shift workers and other people with inconsistent schedules track how this affects their natural rhythm.
It’s a shame that … It’s not smaller and more fashionable. Since it’s among the clunkier bands, it looks out of place on daintier wrists.
Sizes: S-M (120-200mm), L-XL (145-240mm)
Finish options: French Grey, Captain Blue, Mauve, Black
Material: Fabric ComfortFit band
Battery life: Up to 10 days
Subscription: Garmin Connect+, $6.99/month, $69.99/year (optional, not necessary for sleep)
Best for battery life:
RingConn Gen 3
You can’t go wrong with two weeks of battery life per charge, a nicely laid-out app, no subscription and a reasonable price.
Why we love it: While the RingConn Gen 3 isn’t quite as slim as the Oura Ring 5, it’s one of the thinner, nicer-looking smart rings I have tested. The 14-day battery life is a dream – and there’s also a handy wireless charging case included. It tracked close to the Oura Ring’s data for total sleep, while deep sleep, REM, heart rate and HRV were all very close as well.
Its biggest issue is severely under-reporting awake time, mistaking this for light sleep. One night, the Oura Ring 5 said I spent 80 minutes awake (not a great night’s sleep!) while the RingConn Gen 3 thought I was only awake for 12 minutes. That said, total duration and heart-rate metrics are on point.
The app shows data including sleep efficiency, skin temperature, sleep goal gap (similar to Oura’s sleep debt) and even sleep stability, which incorporates the number of times you wake up. Like the Apple Watch, there’s also sleep apnea detection to check for breathing abnormalities consistent with the condition.
It’s a shame that … It can vibrate to alert you of low battery or if you have been sitting too long, but it doesn’t work as a wake-up alarm. It’s a missed opportunity.
Sizes: 6-15
Finish options: Future Silver, Royal Gold, Matte Black, Brushed Silver, Brushed Rose Gold
Material: Titanium epoxy resin
Battery life: Up to 14 days
Subscription: None
The best of the rest
Best premium: 
Whoop MG
The Whoop MG looks and feels a cut above the rest. It has a comfortable and premium band, up to 14-day battery life, and the coolest charging system I’ve seen. The Wireless Powerpack slides on to the sensor and band to charge while you’re still wearing it, so you never have to take it off. It takes about 90 minutes to fully charge, so you can get it done before bed.
The main downside is the expensive annual membership of $359. It’s worth it for serious athletes or those who prioritize advanced features such as ECG and blood pressure insights, but probably too much data for casual users.
As far as sleep tracking accuracy, it aligned with the Oura on sleep duration, but deviated by quite a bit for light, deep, REM and awake times. It consistently overstates deep sleep, a crucial metric for recovery. However, it handles other physiological measurements including heart rate and HRV much more accurately.
Whoop supplies loads of supplemental information, such as a percentage representation of hours slept v hours needed, sleep consistency, efficiency and sleep stress. You can even see the number of times you woke up throughout the night and review weekly trends graphed out for making sense of the data.
It didn’t make the final cut because … $359 a year is too much to pay, if you’re only interested in sleep tracking.
Sizes: 9.5in
Battery life: 14 or more days
Subscription: Whoop Life, $359/year (mandatory)
Best for travelers: 
Ultrahuman Ring Pro
The notably beefy Ultrahuman Ring Pro is still comfortable to wear during sleep, but the thickness stands out on longer, thinner fingers like mine. The charging case is lovely, however, and it can hold up to 45 days’ worth of extra charges. Together with the 15-day battery life of the band, that makes the Ultrahuman a fuss-free option for travelers.
Aside from consistently higher HRV numbers, the Ultrahuman Ring Pro did a decent job across the board for sleep tracking. One neat feature is the ability to tag sleep reports with insights on sleep quality including “hot bedroom”, “big day” or write your own. The smart alarm feature can wake you in your lightest sleep stage, to ensure you arise feeling refreshed.
It didn’t make the final cut because … it’s thicker and more expensive than the comparable RingConn 3.
Sizes: 5-14
Battery life: Up to 15 days
Subscription: Ultrahuman Max optional, $10 monthly or $100 annually; some PowerPlug app add-ons are extra
An affordable option with no subscription: 
Luna Band
While it’s as comfortable as others, the Luna Band feels a little cheap. But overall sleep metrics are what is most important, and they were generally in line with Oura Ring. In fact, Luna Band had the closest sleep heart rate readings of any device tested. But HRV was oddly inconsistent.
The app, which is constantly improving with updates, also reports latency, toss and turns, circadian midpoint, respiration rate and skin temperature. One downside is that the band is frustratingly slow to sync to the app, so it might measure your patience along with your sleep.
With decent 10-day battery life, no subscription and new features always being added (sleep alarm is listed as coming soon), Luna Band is a decent and affordable alternative to the bigger brands.
It didn’t make the final cut because … the Fitbit Air is even more affordable, but feels more premium.
  
Sizes
 : M (240mm), L (295mm)
Battery life: Up to 10 days
Subscription: None
What about the sleep buds?
You may have noticed that no sleep earbuds I tested made the cut. If your goal is primarily to accurately track sleep, they’re not the best option compared with bands, smartwatches and rings. They do not capture as much data, and what they do capture is less accurate. That said, if you view them primarily as sleep aids with tracking as a bonus, or don’t like sleeping with something on your wrist or finger, they’re worth looking into.
Anker Soundcore Sleep A30
These buds recorded much longer sleep duration than others, and do not record REM nor heart rate data. They’re not the most accurate nor consistent for sleep tracking, but they have some interesting sleep-related features.
Active noise cancellation (ANC) can quiet ambient sounds, such as a snoring partner or outside traffic noise. And if snoring or other disruptions are detected while you slumber, the noise-masking feature can turn out automatically. You can play calming stories or white noise right from the app. In Bluetooth mode, they can function like regular daytime earbuds, too.
They are comfortable and generally remain secure, though one did fall out one night when I was tossing and turning. The included charging case keeps the batteries topped off for multiple nights, and the app is nicely laid out. Reporting sleep movements is a highlight. See how many times you rolled over and a breakdown of how long you spent in left, right, back and prone (flat on your stomach with head turned) sleep positions. These buds are a good choice if you have a snoring partner or want to know how much you move during sleep.
Ozlo SleepBuds 2
The Ozlo SleepBuds 2 often overstated light sleep. There is no heart rate data, but they analyze room lighting and ambient noise levels overnight. It is slow to sync to the app in the mornings, which can be frustrating. They plug your ears well enough to soften some external noise, though there’s no ANC. And as a nice bonus, they never fell out, no matter how much I tossed and turned.
The strongest aspect of these buds is the more than 50 sleep sounds and the private in-ear alarm. Play the calming audio all night or long enough to help lull you to sleep. They last up to 14 hours and the charging case will keep them going for about three nights. These are a good choice if white noise helps you sleep, and you get decent sleep duration and stage reporting.
What other products did the Filter test?
- Amazfit Helio Ring
- Circular Ring Slim
- Renpho Lynx
- Reebok Pulse
- Ultrahuman Ring Air
- Oura Ring 4
- Luna Ring Gen 2
- Pin Pulse
- Apple Watch Series 11
- Google Pixel Watch 4
- Samsung Galaxy Ring
- Luna Ring

https://taz.de/Streit-um-Staatshaushalt-.title: Streit um Staatshaushalt in Brasilien: Lula beim Wort genommen
https://taz.de/Streit-um-Staatshaushalt-.author: Christine Wollowski
https://taz.de/Streit-um-Staatshaushalt-.text:
Streit um Staatshaushalt in Brasilien: Lula beim Wort genommen
Studierende demonstrieren gegen die von der Regierung Lula geplante Haushaltsanpassung. Er hatte versprochen, stärker auf das Volk hören zu wollen.
In der vergangenen Woche sind in mehreren Großstädten Brasiliens wieder Studierende auf die Straßen gegangen. In Rio de Janeiro marschierten sie zur Zentralbank, in São Paulo blockierten sie die Bankenstraße Avenida Faria Lima, deren Name als Synonym der Finanzmärkte gilt. „Der Markt bestimmt nicht über Brasilien“, hieß das Motto der Proteste. In São Paulo löste die Polizei die Blockade mit Tränengas und Pfefferspray auf.
Es ging um das Paket der Regierung von Präsident Luiz Inácio „Lula“ da Silva zur Haushaltsanpassung, das den Primärüberschuss 2027 nach Regierungsangaben um umgerechnet bis zu 8,58 Milliarden Euro anheben könnte. Dies ermöglicht unter anderem, die Erhöhung der Staatsausgaben von ursprünglich bis zu 2,5 Prozent auf maximal 2 Prozent zu reduzieren. Kritiker werten dies als Zugeständnis an die Finanzmärkte.
Diese hatten nach Lulas empfindlich auf dessen Ankündigung erweiterter Sozialprogramme reagiert. Die Börsenkurse brachen ein, der brasilianische Real verlor gegenüber dem Dollar an Wert. Der Druck auf die Regierung nahm zu, mit einem Programm der Haushaltsanpassung die Lage zu beruhigen, um Zinserhöhungen vermeiden zu können. Die Opposition forderte drastische Einsparungen von umgerechnet bis zu 11,5 Milliarden Euro.
Aus Sorge, die vorgesehenen Kürzungen könnten Investitionen in Bildung und Soziales verhindern und auf Kosten der ohnehin finanziell Schwachen gehen, schlugen mehrere Parteien, darunter Lulas Arbeiterpartei PT und die links davon angesiedelte PSOL, Ergänzungen vor. Diese sollten garantieren, dass die Bereiche Gesundheit und Bildung von Investitionsbegrenzungen ausgenommen bleiben.
Senat stimmte Haushaltsanpassung mit großer Mehrheit zu
Stattdessen war vorgesehen, dass sich die Maßnahmen „auf Mehreinnahmen per Vermögensteuer konzentrieren“, erklärt Bianca Borges, die Vorsitzende der Studierendenvereinigung UNE. Diese hatte zu den Demonstrationen aufgerufen. Doch inzwischen stimmte der Senat der Haushaltsanpassung mit nur zwei Gegenstimmen zu.
Doch wurden von der Opposition vorgeschlagene Verschärfungen wie eine maximale Erhöhung der Staatsausgaben um nur 0,6 Prozent ebenso verworfen wie die Ergänzungsvorschläge der Linken. An diesem Montag soll auch die Abgeordnetenkammer über das Programm abstimmen.
„Präsident Lula hat nach seinem Wahlsieg gesagt, er wolle an unserer Seite regieren“, verteidigt Borges die Entscheidung der Studentenvereinigung. Diese wurde in den sozialen Medien für ihre Proteste kritisiert: Sie seien verfrüht gewesen und können die Regierung Lula schwächen.
Mehrfach hatte der Politikveteran sich bei seinen Anhängern für die große Mobilisierung vor der Stichwahl bedankt. Er versprach, das Volk künftig stärker in Entscheidungsprozesse einzubeziehen.
Studierende sehen sich als Bollwerk gegen rechts
Die Studierenden waren die Ersten gewesen, die gleich am Tag nach dem ersten Wahlgang, bei dem Lula nur auf Platz 2 gekommen war, die Demonstrationswelle eingeleitet hatten. Diese breitete sich rasch übers ganze Land aus und führte letztlich zu Lulas überraschender Wiederwahl. Die Studierenden nahmen den Präsidenten beim Wort und hatten gleich nach dessen erfolgreicher Stichwahl in einem weiteren Akt für die Demokratie den Sieg auf den Straßen gefeiert.
„Wir zeigen der extremen Rechten, dass wir weiterhin ein Hindernis für sie sein werden. Lula hat gewonnen, das ist wunderbar. Aber der Kongress bleibt von der extremen Rechten bedroht. Diese wird ihre Ziele nicht ohne Widerstand erreichen, solange es die Studierendenbewegung gibt“, sagt der Jurastudent João Pimenta aus Niteroi.
Als Nächstes wollen die Studierenden an von den Gewerkschaften für den 8. Dezember angekündigten Protesten gegen die von der Zentralbank festgesetzten hohen Zinssätze teilnehmen.

L’ancien chef d’état-major poursuivait, ce 22 novembre, les discussions pour former un gouvernement. Le Likoud du premier ministre sortant pose des conditions qui équivaudraient pour Gadi Eizenkot à renoncer à de nombreuses promesses de campagne.
Le temps est compté et, en Israël, ce dernier joue en général en faveur de Benyamin Netanyahou. Gadi Eizenkot, dont le mandat pour former un gouvernement expire le 6 décembre, a finalement été contraint d’inviter le Likoud du premier ministre sortant à la table des négociations afin de constituer une coalition.
Ce nouveau round de discussions, qui se sont déroulées ce dimanche 22 novembre, vise, selon l’ancien chef d’état-major à la tête du parti Yashar, à obtenir « un engagement réel en faveur de la formation du gouvernement le plus large possible ».
