Exhibition of the week
Nan Goldin: You Never Did Anything Wrong 
  
The great chronicler of real American lives fills the Hayward with passion and protest.
 
Hayward Gallery, London, 24 November to 14 March
Also showing
Van Eyck: The Portraits 
  
Jaw-droppingly brilliant paintings that bring you face to face with medieval people.
 
National Gallery, London, from 21 November to 11 April
Bianca Raffaella
 
This partially sighted graduate of Tracey Emin’s art school paints ethereal, shifting veils of whiteness.
 
Flowers Gallery, London, until 2 January
Ragnar Kjartansson
 
Nordic noir from the acclaimed Icelander should suit the moody woodlands of this sculpture trail and gallery.
 
Goodwood Art Foundation, West Sussex, from 26 November to 12 April
Anselm Kiefer 
  
The mighty German who may be the greatest artist alive brings another truckload of his imaginative excess to London.
 
White Cube Bermondsey, London, from 25 November to 24 January
Image of the week
As anxieties around climate catastrophe and existential threats from new technology intensify, humanity turns to mass media to confirm its worst fears. That’s the idea behind this singular German “wonderbook” from the 1550s, which depicts sensationalised scenes of terror in watercolour and gouache. In it, a plague of locusts arrive in Poland on a “terrible wind” in 1527, the North Sea floods Frisia in 1230 and, in the image above, dragons fly over Bavaria in 1533. The Book of Miracles is expected to reach up to £1m at auction at Christies in London, where the public can see it in person before it is sold.
 
What we learned
A Van Gogh masterpiece sold for a record $190.4m after a dispute
Van Eyck’s portraits preserved monsters, merchants – and his wife – like flies in amber
Peggy Guggenheim’s time in London is the focus of a new Royal Academy show
Edward Hopper’s lonesome paintings also depict his sexual issues, says a new book
Palestinian artists looked back in anger, melancholy and defiance at a new exhibition
You can get up close and personal with a Renaissance godfather at the Wallace Collection
Mary Cassatt was a neglected but decisive influence on impressionism
An immersive show brings Kyffin Williams’ rugged Welsh landscapes to life
Masterpiece of the week
Portrait of a Woman by Workshop of the Master of the Holy Kindred, 1495-1500
This face from the past is so alive, as if you met her in the flesh. That’s partly because the unknown artist has posed his unknown subject, who probably lived in Cologne, Germany, looking out of the painting to the side. She seems to be in conversation: there’s a sense of movement, energy, engagement. Then again this mobility must also belong to her, not just the artist’s bag of tricks. For she seems quite a character: her long, thin face, penetrating grey eyes, thin eyebrows and bow-shaped lips all suggest a strong personal presence. Fashionable, discreetly luxurious clothes and jewellery also make it clear she is a woman of substance. This panel was once joined by a hinge to another, with her facing the lost image on the other side of the diptych: but surely her worldly appearance doesn’t fit with it being a religious scene. Rather, she is looking confidently and with some sense of equality at her husband, presumably a wealthy burgher of Cologne.

Richard Avedon’s rarely seen portraits of Hollywood A-listers – in pictures
After consulting on the production of the 1957 musical Funny Face, which was loosely based on his own life as a young photographer, Richard Avedon considered leaving photography behind to pursue film directing. Although he ultimately remained a photographer, his fascination with Hollywood and its ideals endured throughout his life.
Richard Avedon: Hollywood, a new exhibition, brings together more than 120 of Avedon’s iconic and rarely seen photographs of major Hollywood figures, including actors, directors, writers and composers, capturing the allure and influence of the entertainment industry.
The exhibition was curated by the Richard Avedon Foundation and is on view at Gagosian in Beverly Hills, California, through 19 December 2026

https://gothamist.com/news/over-6k-nyc-a.title: Over 6K NYC apartments for homeless people sat vacant in September, city data shows
https://gothamist.com/news/over-6k-nyc-a.author: Karen Yi
https://gothamist.com/news/over-6k-nyc-a.text:
There were more apartments reserved for homeless New Yorkers sitting empty in September than the number of people sleeping outside, city data shows.
That month, there were 6,159 vacant supportive housing units in the city, according to the most recent report released by the Department of Social Services, while the city’s yearly tally of New Yorkers living on the street counted nearly 5,000 people.
It’s the highest number since the city began releasing a monthly vacancy report last November. The abundance of empty space is causing homeless advocates to question whether city and state leaders are doing enough to prioritize housing homeless residents as colder temperatures approach.
“It is a number that should really frighten everyone,” said Craig Hughes, a social worker for Legal Services NYC, which offers low-income New Yorkers free legal help.
“These aren’t numbers that are bureaucratic. They are numbers of places that people could live, which could potentially save their lives,” he said.
Supportive housing units are reserved for homeless New Yorkers who have a mental illness, substance abuse disorder or other special needs. The units receive a mix of city, state and federal funding. Tenants pay no more than 30% of their income toward rent. They receive additional services to help them stay housed, like counseling or case management.
There are more than 42,000 such apartments across the city.
The Supportive Housing Network of New York, an industry group representing 200 providers statewide, said the true number of vacancies is closer to 1,000 apartments or a 2.5% vacancy rate when excluding the units that aren’t rentable because they’re in disrepair, are sealed off or don’t have a referral. The group said the report also includes some state-managed units that aren’t supportive housing.
“Having a vacancy rate is not inherently a bad thing, if we were at a zero percent vacancy or 100% occupancy then the 10,000 people who were approved for supportive housing would have nowhere to go,” said Tierra Labrada, director of policy and advocacy for the network.
Of the more than 6,100 vacant units in September, 4,270 did not have anyone assigned to them, nor anyone in the process of moving in, the data shows. Some of those units are undergoing repairs or renovations after a move-out.
“If we simply focus all of our energy on renovating these supportive housing units, bringing them online, and prioritizing people who are in Safe Havens and living on the streets, we could make an enormous difference in addressing the street homelessness crisis that is plaguing us today,” said Councilmember Lincoln Restler of Brooklyn, who championed the law making vacancy reporting mandatory.
Nearly half of the empty units are overseen by the state’s Office of Mental Health, which controls a large share of the city’s supportive housing stock. Of the 2,753 vacant units overseen by the state, 400 of them had a tenant waiting to move in.
Agency officials said there were various reasons for the vacancies. Residents move out, and it can take a while to fix the unit to ready it for a new tenant. Some people also reject placements that come with intensive services or shared rooms, and there can be bureaucratic delays in the admissions process.
Hughes said providers can often reject applicants for vague reasons and it can take months to move a person found eligible into an empty unit. He said the city also needs to do more to prevent unnecessary evictions that lead to turnover of units.
Justin Mason, a spokesperson for the state Office of Mental Health said officials understand the need to fill as many available beds as possible and are working to reduce delays in the process. “We are taking measures — including regulatory change — that will benefit New Yorkers living with serious mental illness and in need of housing,” he added.
Officials with the city’s Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, which had more than 20% of the vacancies, said about 200 units were available and empty, while others were either involved in legal disputes, had to address violations or were new and waiting for a certificate of occupancy.
“The vast majority are occupied, with less than 2% vacant and available for someone to move in,” said William Fowler, a spokesperson for the agency.
Vacancies in city supportive housing have long plagued the industry, even as the city’s homeless rates remain elevated. In addition to the 5,000 New Yorkers sleeping on streets or in parks and subways, more than 83,000 New Yorkers are sleeping in shelters.
In February, Mayor Zohran Mamdani told Gothamist he would prioritize filling the empty apartments after a brutal stretch of cold killed 29 New Yorkers, some of them homeless. The number of vacant units has nearly doubled since then.
“This administration is committed to addressing the underlying causes of vacancies, cutting unnecessary red tape and streamlining processes so more New Yorkers can access the stable, supportive housing they need,” City Hall spokesperson Sneha Choudhary said in a statement.
A spokesperson for the Department of Social Services said the agency is more quickly making repairs and moved more people into apartments this year than last. Nicholas Jacobelli said the agency maintained a low vacancy rate for the units they oversee.
Hughes said both the city and state needed to look at the vacancy rates as “crisis numbers.”
”You have 6,000 empty apartments, and you have thousands of people on the street and almost record numbers of people in the municipal shelters, it's really hard to really make that make sense,” he said.

https://gothamist.com/news/mamdani-lays-.title: Mamdani lays out plan to close Rikers by 2032, after years of delays
https://gothamist.com/news/mamdani-lays-.author: Ryan Kost
https://gothamist.com/news/mamdani-lays-.text:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s long-awaited plan to close Rikers Island, released Friday, would empty the island’s jails by the end of 2032, moving the detainees held there to four new borough-based jails and three hospital units while turning the island itself over to climate and sustainability projects.
At the center of the plan is a sharp reduction in the city’s jail population over the next several years, to about two-thirds of the current 6,600 — a benchmark some advocates worry may be hard to meet and sustain in the decades ahead.
Even so, the proposal is the clearest sign yet that the first-year mayor intends to keep his campaign promise to shut down one of New York City’s most notorious institutions, known nationally for its chaos and dysfunction.
The effort to close Rikers Island has lurched along for nearly a decade, slowed by a global pandemic, construction delays and a previous mayoral administration that did little to move it forward. In recent years, city leaders acknowledged that they would not meet a legally mandated August 2027 closure deadline, but hadn’t offered a new timeline.
“Our administration is determined to meet our moral and legal obligation to close Rikers Island once and for all,” Mamdani wrote in a letter that opens the plan.
The new buildings, which are underway but years behind schedule, are designed to be safer and more humane, with smaller housing units, better sightlines, natural light and temperature control.
But advocates like Elizabeth Glazer, who helped write the original closure plan as former Mayor Bill de Blasio’s criminal justice director, warn that without broad reform across the Department of Correction, the city “risks merely exporting the violence of Rikers into new ZIP codes when the neighborhood-based facilities are completed.”
At least nine people have died in the Department of Correction’s custody this year, and not all of them on the island. In August, one man died in a new medical treatment outpost at Bellevue Hospital, the first facility to open as part of the replacement system for Rikers. Two others died at borough courthouses.
The administration still needs the City Council to formally adopt the plan. Councilmembers had signaled in September they were drafting a bill that would tie extensions to specific benchmarks and deadlines. Councilmember Sandy Nurse, who sponsored a 2025 law requiring the administration to release Friday’s report, called the plan “the right move.”
She described it as “a pulling together of work that has been agreed to [a] long time ago that just never was prioritized under Eric Adams, and some expansions into key areas that are going to help us achieve the target jail population.”
The plan has also been well-received by advocates briefed on its contents ahead of its release. Zachary Katznelson, executive director of the Independent Rikers Commission, described the previous administration’s approach as “at best all over the map, but very often antagonistic to what we were trying to achieve.” But he said the new plan marked a “return to common sense” that would make New Yorkers safer.
Darren Mack, co-director of Freedom Agenda, which has long pushed to close Rikers, said advocates were excited by the strategy.
“We can finally remove this moral stain from our city, once and for all,” Mack added.
The Mamdani administration acknowledges risks in the strategic plan, calling Rikers a product of its remote location, failing infrastructure and “a culture of dysfunction that has persisted for generations.”
“We will not transfer the historic and endemic failures of Rikers to new locations across New York City,” the plan promises.
Decades of calls for a closure
Calls to close Rikers date back to at least the late 1970s, when then-Mayor Ed Koch first floated the idea of replacing the massive jail complex with smaller jails across the city’s boroughs. Closure gained real traction in the 2010s, inspired in part by the story of Kalief Browder, a Bronx teenager sent to Rikers in 2010 after being accused of stealing a backpack. He spent three years on Rikers, much of that time in solitary confinement. Eventually, his case was dismissed. Browder died by suicide two years later.
By 2017, a commission led by former Chief Judge Jonathan Lippman came to the conclusion that “Rikers must be closed.” De Blasio, who had previously resisted calls to build an entirely new system separate from the island, finally endorsed the project, calling Browder’s death “a wake-up call to this city.” Two years later, the City Council formally voted to move to the new borough-based jails even over fierce opposition from neighborhood groups.
At Rikers, out-of-sight, out of mind is the norm for both people in our custody and our staff.
As all of this played out, human rights abuses at Rikers mounted, and the city entered into a consent decree with a federal court over the use of force on the island. The judge in that case appointed a monitor to track the department's ongoing reform efforts.
“Close Rikers” advocates have long argued that the island itself was central to the dysfunction. The complex, for instance, sits on a gas-emitting former landfill. Buildings can’t be adequately cooled or ventilated. And thousands of cell doors are broken. What’s more, the island can only be reached by a single road, and a trip using public transit can take at least an hour and a half, which presents issues for families, lawyers and those who work there.
“At Rikers, out-of-sight, out of mind is the norm for both people in our custody and our staff,” Correction Commissioner Stanley Richards said in a video released with the plan.
Initially, the closure seemed within reach. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the jail population fell below 4,000 for the first time since the 1940s, the result of unprecedented cooperation between defense attorneys, prosecutors and court administrators to slow the spread of the coronavirus. The progress, however, was short-lived. Under the Adams administration, the jail population rebounded, borough-based jail construction lagged and costs nearly doubled.
Meanwhile, conditions on Rikers have only festered. In January, the federal judge overseeing reforms handed broad control of the jails to a remediation manager, Nicholas Deml.
Reducing the jail population
Under Mamdani’s new plan, the borough-based jail system would come online gradually over the next six years. His administration has taken a few steps already, such as hiring the city’s first "Close Rikers Czar" and opening the Bellevue treatment unit. Two additional hospital units, one in the Bronx and one in Brooklyn, are expected to open by 2028. The first new jail facility would open in Brooklyn in 2029. The others would follow in 2031 and 2032.
Rikers facilities would be emptied and decommissioned as new beds become available. Altogether, the new facilities would have room for 4,500 people.
In order to make the transition work, the city will have to move quickly and forcefully to reduce the jail population. Under the plan, the city is aiming to get the jail population down to no more than 5,500 by the time the Brooklyn facility opens in 2029 — and then to 4,100 by the end of 2032.
In order to hit those figures, the administration is committing $290 million to expand diversion programs, supervised release, re-entry support and faster case processing.
One of the biggest challenges, according to the plan, is the slow pace of the city’s courts. The jail’s population didn’t grow as a result of more arrests, the plan argues, but rather because people are waiting longer for their cases to resolve.
In New York City, the median time between a felony arrest and a case’s final disposition is 431 days, roughly four months longer than in the rest of the state. At least 1,400 Rikers detainees have been awaiting trial for more than a year.
“We do not want any New Yorker to spend a day longer in detention than necessary,” Mamdani said in the release video.
Chief Administrative Judge Joseph Zayas said in a statement included in the plan that the courts “must not accept a status quo that tolerates excessive delay.”
Achieving this sort of population reduction will take cooperation on the scale of what happened during the COVID-19 pandemic, said Glazer, who is also the founder of the Vital City think tank and policy journal.
“In the same way that the police department has CompStat [a public data reporting system] about crime, the city needs to have a kind of jail stat about who’s in jail and why, how many people are coming in, and how long are they staying,” Glazer said. “That’s what drives the jail population, and that has to be looked at every single day.”
The plan itself states the population estimate is “not meant to be a forecast.” While it notes that the new buildings could be adapted for other uses if the jail population were to continue shrinking, it doesn’t say anything about what the city will do if the figure remains above its target.
'Only half the challenge'
In his own letter attached to the plan, Richards, the first formerly incarcerated person to lead the Department of Correction, notes the new facilities “represent only half the challenge.”
“We must also build a safer, more supportive culture within our jails today, so that it is firmly established when we make the transition,” he wrote.
To that end, the plan pledges to replace the island’s 2,450 defective doors, improve sanitary conditions and “reimagine” staff training.
Much of that has been mandated by Deml, the remediation manager, who earlier this year noted that the Department of Correction struggled to perform basic correctional functions. The plan also accounts for a $50 million investment in programming for people in custody that Deml had recommended.
Christopher Rodriguez’s death at Bellevue in August illustrates the shortcomings of DOC training and protocol, regardless of facility. According to a Board of Correction report obtained by Gothamist, officers at the new unit had skipped required overnight tours in the time before the 36-year-old was found unresponsive. Six officers were suspended.
Unions will be central to any reform, and the plan names the Correction Officers' Benevolent Association as a partner, noting the department has successfully worked with unions in the past to improve working conditions. COBA President Benny Boscio did not respond to requests for comment.
Nurse, the councilmember, blamed the union for years of stalled reform, but noted the remediation manager has the power to circumvent it.
“We have the right conditions right now,” Nurse said, adding that the mayor and the City Council are aligned.
“If we fail to do this, if we fail to successfully transition to these borough-based jails, it will be a huge embarrassment to the city,” Nurse said.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Orçamento de 2027 do RS avança sob críticas do PT e alerta de risco de atraso nos pagamentos
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Mesmo com parecer favorável aprovado na Comissão de Finanças, Planejamento, Fiscalização e Controle da Assembleia Legislativa do Rio Grande do Sul (ALRS), por nove votos a três, o projeto de orçamento do estado para 2027 tem votação em plenário prevista para 1º de dezembro. A proposta não cumpriu o prazo regimental para entrar na pauta de terça-feira (24).
A bancada do Partido dos Trabalhadores (PT) votou contra o projeto e questionou a divergência entre o déficit de R$ 4,87 bilhões previsto pelo atual governo e a projeção de até R$ 7,47 bilhões apresentada pelo relator, deputado estadual Claudio Branchieri (PL), que será secretário da Fazenda do governador eleito Luciano Zucco (PL).
“Há duas verdades ou duas grandes mentiras para o povo gaúcho. E as duas sinalizam uma encrenca gigantesca para o Estado”, afirmou o líder da bancada do PT, deputado estadual Miguel Rossetto. Ele salientou que o próprio relator prevê dificuldades de caixa a partir do segundo semestre, com risco de atraso no pagamento de fornecedores, salários, precatórios e dívida pública.
A bancada do PT também justificou o voto contrário pela avaliação de que o orçamento não garante os mínimos constitucionais de 12% para a saúde e 25% para a educação e pelo risco de atraso nos salários dos servidores apontado pelo relator. “O pagamento em dia dos salários é inegociável para nós”, ressaltou o deputado. A bancada também apresentou emendas para assegurar a aplicação mínima de 12% em saúde, cobrir a insuficiência de R$ 426 milhões apontada pelos parlamentares e corrigir perdas inflacionárias de mais de 30 mil servidores estaduais, acumuladas desde 2015.
Das 1.990 emendas parlamentares protocoladas, o relator acolheu 1.915. Outras 16 receberam parecer contrário, 41 foram consideradas prejudicadas e 18 foram retiradas. As 112 emendas de relatoria foram aprovadas por unanimidade.
Logo após a leitura do parecer por Branchieri, ocorreu a defesa das emendas parlamentares com pedidos de destaque, encaminhados pela bancada do PT. As propostas tratavam da aplicação do mínimo constitucional de 12% na saúde; da destinação ao Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) de R$ 110 milhões previstos para emendas individuais, para alcançar esse percentual; e dos salários de servidores de escolas públicas, cujos vencimentos estão congelados e, em alguns casos, abaixo do piso regional. Todos os destaques foram rejeitados pelo colegiado.
Parecer aponta riscos para as contas de 2027
Conforme o relator, a receita total estimada no Projeto de Lei (PL) 409/2026 é de R$ 95,13 bilhões, e as despesas totais estão fixadas em R$ 99,19 bilhões, uma diferença de R$ 4,06 bilhões. Já o déficit primário previsto é de R$ 4,87 bilhões. Segundo o parecer, o projeto não indica fontes concretas para cobrir o déficit: o artigo 5º diz apenas que a cobertura “será perseguida” com receitas adicionais, controle de despesas e medidas do Regime de Recuperação Fiscal ou de outro instrumento de ajuste com a União.
A avaliação destaca que “não há folga em nenhum indicador” e que “cortes não resolvem”. Dos R$ 99,19 bilhões em despesas, R$ 95,06 bilhões (95,8%) são considerados rígidos: pessoal, dívida, reservas, fontes vinculadas, mínimos constitucionais, despesas contratuais e orçamentos dos demais Poderes.
O parecer apontou que, a partir de junho de 2027, o estado poderá não conseguir pagar simultaneamente a folha dos servidores, os fornecedores, os precatórios e a dívida com a União. Branchieri, porém, voltou atrás e descartou a possibilidade de novos atrasos salariais em entrevista à Rádio Gaúcha Serra nesta segunda-feira (23), conforme publicou o Pioneiro.
Na avaliação do relator, caso não haja acordo com o governo federal para adesão ao Programa de Pleno Pagamento de Dívidas dos Estados (Propag), o novo governo precisará obter uma liminar no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) para suspender ou reescalonar os pagamentos da dívida a partir de junho do próximo ano.
Branchieri encaminhou oito recomendações ao Poder Executivo e, ao final do parecer, reconheceu que o voto favorável não afasta os riscos expostos no relatório, apenas cumpre as exigências de elaboração do orçamento.

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/20.title: Since 2020, the Canon Has Grown Bigger Than Ever Before. Will Museums and the Market Continue to Listen?
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/20.author: Alex Greenberger
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/20.text:
Art history does not divide itself easily into decades, let alone into centuries or even eras, and that makes the 2020s so far a pretty unusual period of time. Not long into 2020, the world was shut down by the Covid pandemic. What followed from there was more chaos: wars in Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan, and elsewhere; two Trump administrations; culture wars around the world; and economic upheaval that has touched all corners of the world, including the art world.
And yet, not all has been bad. During Art Week NYC, a festival held earlier this month by ARTnews, Art in America, and Artforum, ARTnews convened art historian and curator Joseph L. Underwood along with Art in America deputy editor Emily Watlington to discuss the decade so far. Both agreed that some good has resulted, particularly when it comes to the art historical canon. But it remains unclear whether those changes will leave a permanent mark on the art world.
“We’ve recovered a lot of individual figures that have totally deserved [a spotlight], and I’m looking forward to how we can now use that research and rediscovery to tell different stories about art history,” Watlington said.
Underwood noted that this impulse was already underway pre-2020 and pointed to scholarship by historians such as Chika Okeke-Agulu, who published an influential book on Nigerian modernism in 2015. “There have been articles and books about single artists, but there hasn’t been that kind of interconnectivity,” he said. “That’s what was starting, and there is still some of it in art history. But museums and the market have cooled on it.”
That trend, he added, is evident when looking at the past few Venice Biennale editions. The 2022 edition, curated by Cecilia Alemani, contained many female Surrealists; the 2024 edition, organized by Adriano Pedrosa, presented a global view of modernism. “That cooled off in 2026,” he said, referring to Koyo Kouoh’s recently concluded exhibition, which had fewer dead and under-recognized artists.
“It’s certainly been a decade of two steps forward, one step back,” Watlington said. “Change the number of steps!”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Casos de mpox aumentam 156% no DF em novembro; parlamentar cobra plano distrital de vacinação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Ana Gonçalves
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O Distrito Federal chegou a 59 casos confirmados de mpox em 2026, segundo informativo da Secretaria de Saúde (SES-DF) divulgado em 21 de novembro. O número representa um aumento de 156,5% em relação aos 23 registros contabilizados na primeira semana do mês. Diante do crescimento das infecções e de questionamentos sobre a disponibilidade de vacinas, o deputado distrital Fábio Felix (Psol) apresentou um requerimento à Câmara Legislativa (CLDF) cobrando explicações do governo sobre a política de prevenção e o atendimento aos pacientes.
O Requerimento nº 3.133/2026 solicita que a Secretaria de Saúde informe o número de casos por mês e região administrativa, além da quantidade de internações e óbitos. O documento também questiona a existência de um plano distrital de vacinação e pede informações sobre o estoque de imunizantes, a previsão de chegada de novas doses e a quantidade de pessoas que aguardam a primeira ou a segunda aplicação.
De acordo com o boletim epidemiológico divulgado em 16 de novembro, quando o DF contabilizava 51 casos, 45 eram de moradores da capital. Todos os registros daquele levantamento eram de pessoas do sexo masculino, com predominância da faixa etária entre 30 e 39 anos. Até 20 de novembro, não havia registro de mortes pela doença no Distrito Federal.
Interrupção da vacinação
Na justificativa do requerimento, Fábio Félix afirma que o Distrito Federal está sem imunizantes na rede pública e aponta que a interrupção foi comunicada pela própria Secretaria de Saúde em memorando circular de 3 de novembro “por inexistência de doses em estoque”. Segundo o parlamentar, a SES-DF informou que novos lotes haviam sido solicitados ao Ministério da Saúde, mas ainda não havia previsão de quando os imunizantes seriam recebidos.
O deputado também relaciona a interrupção da campanha ao crescimento das infecções no território. Ao recuperar dados divulgados pela Secretaria em 4 de novembro, o requerimento destaca que o DF já contabilizava 23 casos confirmados naquele momento, oito deles registrados apenas em outubro. O documento lembra ainda que, desde 2022, quando começou a disseminação mundial da doença, o Distrito Federal havia acumulado 425 casos confirmados. A justificativa também chama atenção para a circulação do vírus e informa que, à época, o Laboratório Central de Saúde Pública do DF (Lacen-DF) realizava análises complementares para identificar a cepa predominante entre os casos recentes.
Na avaliação apresentada pelo parlamentar, a falta de imunizantes preocupa especialmente porque a vacinação é direcionada a grupos com maior vulnerabilidade à doença. O documento explica que a imunização não é oferecida à população em geral, mas restrita a pessoas vivendo com HIV em estágio de imunossupressão avançada, profissionais expostos e contatos de casos suspeitos ou confirmados, mediante avaliação técnica prévia. Sobre a assistência a esse público, Fábio Felix afirma que se trata justamente da parcela da população com maior risco de evolução grave da doença e destaca: “segundo a própria Secretaria, não há tratamento específico disponível na rede, sendo a atenção voltada ao alívio dos sintomas”. Na sequência, acrescenta: “Nesse cenário, a vacina representa a principal ferramenta de proteção desse público”.
O requerimento também questiona se a Secretaria solicitou a reposição das doses ao Ministério da Saúde antes do esgotamento do estoque. Para fundamentar a cobrança, o parlamentar menciona um ofício enviado pelo governo federal em 29 de setembro, no qual, segundo o documento, o Ministério informou que a estratégia nacional de vacinação contra a mpox permanecia vigente e que o Programa Nacional de Imunizações (PNI) atendia às demandas dos estados e do Distrito Federal. A justificativa aponta que essa informação torna necessário esclarecer se a SES-DF comunicou a necessidade de reposição em tempo hábil. O texto considera “imprescindível esclarecer se a SES-DF comunicou tempestivamente a necessidade de reposição antes do esgotamento do estoque”.
Entre os questionamentos encaminhados à Secretaria estão a quantidade de doses recebidas e aplicadas desde o início da vacinação, a data em que o estoque se esgotou e a previsão de chegada de novos lotes. Fábio Félix também pergunta quantas pessoas aguardam a primeira ou a segunda dose e se existe a possibilidade de ampliar a imunização para outros grupos com maior exposição ao vírus, como usuários da profilaxia pré-exposição ao HIV (PrEP), ou disponibilizá-la em outras unidades além do Hospital Universitário de Brasília (HUB).
Atendimento e prevenção
Além da vacinação, o requerimento cobra informações sobre o tratamento oferecido na rede pública, incluindo as unidades de referência e o acesso a medicamentos antivirais para pacientes com quadros graves. O deputado também solicita esclarecimentos sobre as ações de comunicação em saúde realizadas pelo GDF para informar a população sobre o aumento dos casos, os sintomas, as formas de prevenção e os locais de atendimento. O documento pergunta, ainda, se houve campanhas específicas para comunicar a suspensão da vacinação.
Na justificativa, Fábio Felix menciona que o Centro Brasiliense de Defesa dos Direitos Humanos (CentroDH) e o Estruturação, Grupo LGBT+ de Brasília, acionaram, em 4 de novembro, a Secretaria de Saúde, o Ministério Público do Distrito Federal e Territórios (MPDFT) e o Ministério Público de Contas do DF (MPC-DF), solicitando a apuração das circunstâncias do desabastecimento e medidas para restabelecer a vacinação. As organizações também defenderam a ampliação do acesso aos imunizantes para pessoas LGBT+ em situação de maior exposição, como usuários de PrEP.
Ao justificar a necessidade das informações, o parlamentar afirma que os esclarecimentos são indispensáveis para compreender “as causas do desabastecimento, a previsão de reposição das doses, a cobertura dos grupos prioritários, a capacidade de diagnóstico e a assistência oferecida aos pacientes”. O requerimento busca subsidiar a fiscalização da política distrital de enfrentamento à mpox e possíveis medidas legislativas.
O Brasil de Fato DF procurou a Secretaria de Saúde do Distrito Federal (SES-DF) para esclarecer a situação do estoque de vacinas, a eventual suspensão da imunização e as medidas adotadas diante do aumento de casos. Também foram solicitadas informações sobre o atendimento aos pacientes e a previsão de chegada de novos imunizantes. Até a publicação desta reportagem, a pasta não havia respondido aos questionamentos.

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/fa.title: Faurschou Ends Its Public Exhibition Program as Its New York Space Heads for Demolition
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/fa.author: Tessa Solomon
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/fa.text:
When Faurschou New York opened in 2019, the New York Times compared it to major collector-founded institutions like the Hill Art Foundation, the FLAG Art Foundation, and the Brant Foundation. But unlike those institutions, Faurschou New York was not a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. It also never quite lived up to its lofty expectations.
In March 2025, Faurschou, which was founded as a private art museum and art consultancy in Copenhagen in 1986, announced that the New York outpost was closed “for renovations.” It never reopened. The Greenpoint building that housed it was sold in June to a developer, city records show, and the city has approved its demolition. A condominium planned for the site cements what founder and art collector Jens Faurschou himself announced in April: After four decades, Faurschou’s public exhibitions are over.
The building at 148-150 Green Street, once home to Faurschou New York and the restaurant Ilis, was sold at the end of June to the developer Investmates for $25.55 million, according to city property records reviewed by ARTnews. The seller, Green Art Holdings LLC, bought it in 2017 for $18 million, according to Commercial Observer. On October 27, the Department of Buildings approved its full demolition, according to city records. Investmates plans a seven-story, 73-unit condominium on the site, Crain’s reported.
In a statement posted to the company’s website, Jens Faurschou said that with the closing of the New York space he was “bringing the public exhibition program to an end.” After 40 years, he wrote, his “direction changes”: He will focus on his family, private dealing, and working with artists, institutions, and collections. The statement does not clarify what will become of the collection, or whether the Copenhagen and Beijing spaces remain operational.
Faurschou staged solo exhibitions of artists from Tracey Emin to Shirin Neshat and Danh Vo, and showed works by Robert Rauschenberg and Louise Bourgeois. Programming at its global locations appeared to have stopped years earlier: Copenhagen last listed an exhibition in 2018 and Beijing in 2021-22, according to the company’s website and exhibition listings.
Its 12,000-square-foot New York space last hosted an exhibition of work by the Chinese artist Ai Weiwei, which ended in February 2025. As of late October 2025, the exhibition appeared to still be installed, visible through the windows. Neither the artist’s studio nor Faurschou responded to a request for comment at that time.
His statement did not address the company’s finances, which have come under scrutiny in recent years. An auditor warned about its accounts, and a court issued a bankruptcy order against Faurschou ApS in November 2025 that was canceled two weeks later.
A degree of mystery surrounds the Danish art dealer, dubbed the “Don Corleone of art” in a 2016 Politiken profile. By his account, his career began in 1984, the year he traveled to New York City and made his first art deal—a few Fluxus works, sold at the suggestion of Art Library founder Knud Pedersen. That same year, he met his future first wife, Luise Faurschou. The two married in 1985 and soon after opened Galleri Faurschou on Store Strandstræde.
According to the profile, the gallery maintained a small but respectable stable of artists—Christian Lemmerz, Nina Sten-Knudsen, Erik A. Frandsen, and Michael Kvium—while also handling blue-chip works. “I sold Warhol,” he recalled. “I sold Poliakoff, I sold Picasso, lots of Picassos. The biggest deal I made, which was the most fun, was around 2004. It was a package of five Picassos and two Mirós.” In 2012, he and Luise relocated the business to Nordhavn, which he continued to run alone following their divorce.
The Faurschou collection underpins his business, but in interviews, he has declined to specify its scope, value, and exact ownership. In 2016, he compared himself to collectors who “have a showroom and a big collection. And sell something from time to time to be able to buy something else.” He claimed to have purchased a monumental work from Robert Rauschenberg, which he said he would part with only for the Museum of Modern Art in New York. (There is no public record that MoMA owns a Rauschenberg that was sold or donated by Jens Faurschou. However, Mirthday Man, a work from the Faurschou collection, was shown in a 2017 Rauschenberg exhibition at MoMA.)
Also listed in his collection are works by Louise Bourgeois, Cai Guo-Qiang, Danh Vo, Shirin Neshat, and Bill Viola, as well as a substantial number of pieces by Ai Weiwei. He told Politiken the value of the collection “depends on whether it’s a good or a bad day,” and that he is an art dealer but that he “no longer” runs a gallery that represents artists and sells their works.
A 2024 article in the Danish-language outlet Børsen described Faurschou’s business model as including a “philanthropic” part, which stages “non-commercial” exhibitions. His philanthropic activities, the report notes, include helping establish the art center and nonprofit organization Copenhagen Contemporary. When he opened his Brooklyn location in 2019, Faurschou told the New York Times that he occasionally sells works from his private collection and does consulting work to finance his free exhibitions. According to Børsen, however, his business is financed by wealthy, unnamed individuals, who also finance and own the art. In 2025, Jyllands-Posten estimated that the collection comprises roughly 400 works.
Faurschou has said that these non-commercial shows have cost him several million DKK over the years. The Politiken profile notes that several of Faurschou’s companies narrowly sidestepped going into the red in 2015, after the sale of several properties in Taastrup. The art dealer said he was “absolutely” generating funds from the collection to remedy the shortfall.
Jyllands-Posten reported in 2025 that with a loss exceeding DKK 25 million ($3.6 million) in 2024, his holding company, Faurschou Holding ApS, had amassed total losses of nearly DKK 174 million ($25.3 million) since its founding in 2012. Company accounts show equity has been negative for six straight years, standing at a deficit of DKK 154 million ($22.4 million) as of 2024. Given these circumstances, the auditor expressed doubts about the value of the art Faurschou has purchased, noting that there was “significant uncertainty about the valuation of the company’s assets.”
The 2023 accounts were similarly fraught. Børsen reported in 2024 that despite his industry renown, “the seasoned art dealer has blood-red accounts, where virtually no values are registered.” Faurschou also had a dispute with an auditor from Deloitte, who at the time questioned his business model. According to the article, the auditor wrote that the company accounts “do not give a true and fair view of the companies’ liabilities, assets and financial position, and in addition, the auditor does not believe in the companies’ future operations.”
The report added: “Because there is no faith in the future operations, the auditor also calls the management report incorrect, as it assumes continued operations.”
This credit history painted a tense backdrop for the company’s brush with bankruptcy. On November 6, 2025, the Probate Court of the Maritime and Commercial Court in Denmark issued a bankruptcy order for Faurschou ApS, only to cancel it on November 20. The cancelation ended the legal process that would have seized the company’s assets and operations, because the legal threshold for bankruptcy was no longer met.
Public records also show legal claims on Faurschou’s own property. Notices in Statstidende say Møns Bank asked a court to auction two properties he owns, a house in Humlebæk and a summer house in Nysted, with sales set for May. As of November 23, the land registry still listed him as the owner of the Humlebæk house. Separately, the registry shows the Danish Tax Administration placed liens on that house on April 23 totaling about DKK 8.5 million, or roughly $1.3 million.
For his part, Faurschou had expressed confidence in the future of his company, telling Børsen in 2024: “I have tried to explain to the accountant why I see it differently than he does, but I absolutely cannot blame him for what he writes, because the requirements for an accountant are much higher today than they were before.” He said the company was working on “large and complex projects,” the details of which he could not share at the time. He added that, alongside the “philanthropic” part of his business, there was an “income-generating” side, where he acted as a broker for major art dealers and facilitated sales from the company’s collection. His April statement does not indicate whether his plans to focus on private dealing include that brokerage and those collection sales.
Reports have left unclear the exact nature of Faurschou’s operations, and the terms used to describe it have shifted over the years between “foundation” and “private museum.”
“You call [Faurschou] a foundation, but it’s not a trust, is it,” Politiken asked. Faurschou replied, “No, but neither is the Tryg Foundation,” referencing the charitable arm of TryghedsGruppen, a Danish holding company that is the largest shareholder of the insurance company Tryg. He confirmed that his business is a limited company and explained that the use of the word “foundation” signals that the art on view is not for sale. Visitors “expect to come into a place where there [are] no sales” being conducted, he said, adding that this also ensured employees at the front desk were not asked about the price list.
When pressed further, he stressed that at least the Copenhagen operation “absolutely” was philanthropic, but did not elaborate on the specifics of the philanthropy. “It’s just that not many people take advantage of the philanthropic offer,” he said.
Faurschou launched its Greenpoint, Brooklyn, space in 2019 to great fanfare. Mads Refslund, the Scandinavian chef who cofounded Copenhagen’s Noma with René Redzepi, opened Ilis New York in a space attached to Faurschou. (Refslund is reportedly close with Jens Faurschou and his wife, Marsha, with one source saying he contributed to their wedding menu.) The opening of Ilis, packed with art world regulars, was similarly tasteful: employees’ uniforms were designed by Camilla Staerk and Lady and Butler’s founder Eli Caner. The restaurant closed in May 2026, citing the building’s sale; Refslund told Eater that he and a group of investors had tried to buy the building, but were outbid by a developer.
In his closing remark, Jens Faurschou described the whole venture, across four cities, as a “program of cross-cultural dialogue.”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Justiça suspende pesquisa mineral em serras de Itarantim e impõe multas de até R$ 100 mil por danos
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Observatório Rio Pardo
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A Justiça da Bahia aceitou, em 13 de novembro de 2026, o pedido de urgência feito pelo Ministério Público do Estado (MPBA) para parar atividades de pesquisa mineral nas serras de Itarantim. A ação civil pública cita quatro empresas ligadas ao projeto de pesquisa de terras raras e nióbio denominado “Projeto Itarantim” e a decisão determina a paralisação imediata das atividades das empresas nas áreas dos Monumentos Naturais instituídos pela Lei Municipal, de iniciativa popular, nº 010/2025. A decisão judicial é um desdobramento do conflito mineral iniciado em 2024 no município, quando comunidades impediram uma empresa de realizar procedimentos, denunciando a atuação sem a autorização de proprietários.
As empresas Cacto Geologia Mineração e Meio Ambiente Ltda., Niobium Brazil Importação e Exportação Ltda., Ionic Clays Brazil Ltda. e IMC Rare Earths Participações Ltda. deverão cessar imediatamente toda a atividade de pesquisa, prospecção, intervenções, exploraçao ou extração mineral nas poligonais dos monumentos da lei municipal.
A proibição abrange perfurações, sondagens de qualquer natureza, trincheiras, poços, coleta de amostras, abertura ou alargamento de acessos, além de supressão vegetal, terraplanagem e intervenções em cursos d’água. Também ficam proibidos o ingresso e a permanência de máquinas, sondas, veículos de perfuração e equipes técnicas no perímetro para fins de pesquisa.
A decisão ainda fixou o prazo de 5 dias para a retirada de todos os equipamentos que estejam nas áreas protegidas, comprovando a desmobilizaçao em até 48 horas, e o restabelecimento do fluxo hídrico do córrego interrompido nas comunidades do Palmeiras e Córgão e demais córregos afetados em até 15 dias, obrigando as empresas a apresentarem o relatório georreferenciado de todas as intervenções físicas realizadas no território municipal desde 2023, detalhando todas as informações técnicas.
Para garantir o cumprimento, o juiz fixou multa diária de R$ 50 mil para cada empresa em caso de descumprimento da proibição, além de multa de R$ 100 mil por cada ato de intervenção física ou perfuração constatado após a intimação. Autorizou, ainda, que oficiais de justiça realizem apreensão e remoção de máquinas e equipamentos encontrados em atividade ilícita, com requisição de força policial militar se necessário.
A validade da Lei de iniciativa popular
O advogado Clodoaldo Silva (Ceas) explica que esta decisão ainda não se trata de uma sentença definitiva, mas de uma decisão liminar: “concedida antes mesmo da manifestação das empresas”. Contudo, destaca que: “essa é uma importante vitória jurídica das comunidades que lutam contra a mineração nesses territórios”.
Ele explica que um dos pontos fundamentais desse processo foi “a decisão de reconhecer a legitimidade do município para estabelecer restrições ambientais à qualquer atividade minerária, especialmente para proteger as serras, nascentes e mananciais responsáveis pelo abastecimento da população”.
Essa fundamentação está amparada está amparada nos arts. 23, 30 e 225 da Constituição Federal e no Tema 145 do ST, que dipoem do dever municipal de proteger a natureza e o direito de criar leis ambientais próprias. De acordo com o STF, essas leis municipais são válidas desde que se tratem de um interesse local, como no caso de Itarantim.
O documento ainda aponta que as empresas não possuíam licenciamento ambiental do Inema para a realização da pesquisa mineral, e que o alvará de pesquisa dado pela Agência Nacional de Mineração (ANM) não as exime de cumprir as legislações estaduais e municipais.
Por fim, a decisão reconhece o que as comunidades vinham denunciando acerca da continuidade da pesquisa mineral, mesmo após a suspensão emitida pela Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente em abril de 2026, revogada no mês de setembro.
A luta continua
Embora seja uma vitória importante, as comunidades reconhecem que é necessário continuar a mobilização para o efetivo cumprimento da lei. A Comissão Popular de Meio Ambiente aguarda a intimação das quatro empresas e acompanham o processo, uma vez que as empresas devem recorrer da decisão.
Essa vitória é importante porque mostra que a articulação e a mobilização popular são importantes barreiras para limitar a especulação internacional e o avanço dos processos minerários em torno de minerais estratégicos, uma vez que o Brasil, em particular a Bahia possui grande diversidade desses elementos.
O caso também pode servir de exemplo para outros municípios da Bacia do Rio Pardo e do Rio Jequitinhonha que estão sendo ameaçados pela mineração. A liminar não encerra a disputa, mas cria um precedente importante, motivado por um processo popular de defesa do direito à água e ao território.

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/ly.title: Lynette Yiadom-Boakye and Anne Imhof Make Vogue’s 2026 Best-Dressed List
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/ly.author: Hikmat Mohammed
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/ly.text:
As the year comes to an end, it’s that time when glossy titles publish their annual best-dressed lists—actors and musicians are to be expected, naturally. On Monday, Vogue US and British Vogue published their lists simultaneously, featuring A-list stars such as Zendaya, Kendall Jenner, Greta Lee, Sarah Pidgeon and more. Artists were also named, although few and far among them were British painter and writer Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, artist and choreographer Anne Imhof, and architect Sumayya Vally.
Vogue US selected 55 individuals for its best-dressed lists, while British Vogue handpicked 50. Yiadom-Boakye and Vally made it to British Vogue’s list, and Imhof was paired with her partner, the dancer Devon Teuscher, by Vogue US.
Imhof and Teuscher were described as “Berghain Romeo and Juliet” by Vogue US, and the publication said 2026 was their year because of Imhof’s queer, Shakespearean solo exhibition “House of Swans,” which features a four-act ballet. Last year’s Vogue US list featured artist and New York’s First Lady Rama Duwaji. Vogue US could not be reached for a comment at time of publication.
British Vogue’s best-dressed list applauded Yiadom-Boakye for her “eclectic” style. The magazine compared the artist’s style to the characters featured in her portraits, where “clothes naturally play a crucial role,” but argued that “while the fashion that features in her art never feels too hooked to a particular time or place, the clothes in her real-world wardrobe couldn’t feel more now.”
Another name on the list was Vally, the architect who will be designing French-Lebanese philanthropist Elie Khouri’s contemporary art foundation, the Elie Khouri Art Foundation. The magazine described Vally as “hardly your typical fashion girlie” and that her signature look is her “slinky, head-to-toe black and statement winged eyeliner.” The architect is also a fixture on the front row of runway shows, from Hermès to Roksanda and Harris Reed. British Vogue could not be reached for a comment at time of publication.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Encontro em Porto Alegre debate falhas na rede de proteção às mulheres e no enfrentamento aos feminicídios
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Mesmo quando conseguem uma medida protetiva de urgência, muitas mulheres continuam expostas à violência e ao risco de feminicídio no Rio Grande do Sul. A distância entre a garantia prevista na legislação e a proteção efetivamente oferecida pelo Estado estará no centro do encontro “Diálogos sobre violências e feminicídios – Dados, visões e convergências no RS”, que acontece nesta terça-feira (24), às 13h30, no auditório da Defensoria Pública do Estado, em Porto Alegre (Rua Múcio Teixeira, 110, 9º andar).
A atividade integra a programação dos 21 Dias de Ativismo pelo Fim da Violência contra as Mulheres e reunirá representantes de movimentos sociais, organizações de mulheres, universidades, instituições públicas e veículos de comunicação. O Brasil de Fato RS está entre as convidadas para participar das discussões. A jornalista Fabiana Reinholz integra a primeira mesa, que abordará os indicadores de violência de gênero e os desafios na produção e no tratamento dos dados.
Segundo os dados reunidos pela organização até 18 de novembro, a Secretaria da Segurança Pública do Rio Grande do Sul registrava 73 feminicídios em 2026, enquanto o Observatório de Feminicídios Lupa Feminista contabilizava 80 casos. Em 2025, os registros oficiais apontaram 80 feminicídios, diante de 92 casos identificados pelo observatório. A análise dos indicadores e dos diferentes critérios de registro será um dos pontos de partida para discutir as respostas do Estado.
O evento é promovido pelo Núcleo Interdisciplinar de Estudos sobre Mulher e Gênero da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (Niem/UFRGS), Articuladoras Territoriais de Políticas para as Mulheres (Ministério das Mulheres, ONU Mulheres e PNUD), Conselho Estadual dos Direitos da Mulher do RS, Observatório de Feminicídios Lupa Feminista e Querela Jornalistas Feministas. Em parceria com o Comitê Latino-Americano e do Caribe para a Defesa dos Direitos das Mulheres (Cladem Brasil), Coletivo Feminino Plural, Associação das Promotoras Legais Populares, Levante Feminista Contra o Feminicídio, Lesbocídio e Transfeminicídio e Sindicato de Jornalistas Profissionais do RS, entre outras entidades. E apoio do Núcleo de Defesa da Mulher (Nudem) da Defensoria Pública do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul.
Medidas protetivas não garantem, por si só, a segurança das mulheres
Um dos dados levantados para o encontro indica que cerca de uma em cada quatro mulheres vítimas de feminicídio no estado já havia solicitado medida protetiva de urgência. O dado, conforme aponta a organizção do evento, coloca em discussão a efetividade dos mecanismos previstos na Lei Maria da Penha e a capacidade do poder público de acompanhar situações em que a ameaça permanece mesmo após a intervenção judicial.
“O debate examina o que ocorre entre o pedido e a proteção efetiva, com atenção à fiscalização das medidas, à atuação das Patrulhas Maria da Penha e à comunicação entre os serviços de atendimento, as forças de segurança e o sistema de justiça”, afirma Télia Negrão, representante do Ministério das Mulheres no RS.
Outro eixo será a prevenção da violência de gênero. As discussões devem abordar a aplicação da legislação gaúcha que prevê o trabalho sobre violência contra as mulheres nas escolas e as possibilidades de enfrentar padrões culturais que naturalizam a violência.
Também estará em pauta o relatório da Comissão Especial de Combate ao Feminicídio da Assembleia Legislativa, que identifica lacunas na rede de proteção e recomenda a ampliação de recursos para serviços como casas-abrigo, centros de referência e programas de reabilitação de agressores.
Mesas discutem dados, experiências e políticas de enfrentamento
A programação começa às 13h30, com a abertura das entidades promotoras. Às 14h, a primeira mesa, “O que os dados nos dizem?”, reunirá representantes de instituições públicas, observatórios, organizações da sociedade civil e veículos de comunicação para discutir os indicadores de violência contra as mulheres no Rio Grande do Sul, as lacunas na produção e integração de informações e os desafios para transformar os dados em políticas públicas.
Entre as participantes estão Andrea Rezende Russo, coordenadora da Coordenadoria Estadual da Mulher em Situação de Violência Doméstica do Tribunal de Justiça do RS; o coronel Alexandre Moojen, do Observatório de Violência contra a Mulher da Secretaria da Segurança Pública; Thaís Pereira Siqueira, do Observatório de Feminicídios Lupa Feminista; e Juliane Lorencena Chassot, perita criminal e coordenadora do Núcleo de Perícias em Feminicídio do Instituto-Geral de Perícias (Nupefem/IGP).
A mesa também contará com a participação de jornalistas. Fabiana Reinholz, do Brasil de Fato RS, e Valéria Ochoa, do jornal Extra Classe, foram convidadas para contribuir com o debate. Também participa Teresa Cristina Bruel dos Santos, do Coletivo Feminino Plural. A coordenação será da professora Cibele Cheron, do Núcleo Interdisciplinar de Estudos sobre Mulher e Gênero da UFRGS (Niem/UFRGS).
Às 15h15, a segunda mesa, “Diferentes olhares, uma realidade”, abordará as experiências de mulheres e organizações que atuam no enfrentamento às violências, considerando as desigualdades raciais, sociais e territoriais. Participam representantes de organizações de mulheres indígenas, negras, ciganas, quilombolas e de movimentos de defesa dos direitos das mulheres.
Entre as convidadas estão Sueli de Oliveira Tomas, da Articulação Nacional das Mulheres Indígenas Guerreiras da Ancestralidade (ANMIGA); a cacica Kerexu Takuá, do Centro de Referência Indígena do RS; Lucélia Gomes da Silva, do Sempre Mulher Instituto de Pesquisa e Intervenção sobre Relações Raciais; Maria Conceição Lopes Fontoura, da Maria Mulher Organização de Mulheres Negras; Estela Oliveira, da Associação das Promotoras Legais Populares; Virginia Vanessa Astigarraga Bonaldo, da Associação Ciganos Itinerantes do RS; e Mãe Patty de Oxum, defensora popular do Quilombo do Ouro, na Lomba do Pinheiro.
A mesa será coordenada por Lilian Conceição da Silva, articuladora territorial do Ministério das Mulheres, e terá como debatedoras Jéssica Miranda Pinheiro, diretora executiva da Themis – Gênero, Justiça e Direitos Humanos, e Luisa Horn Silveira, da Clínica Feminista e Interseccional da UFRGS.
Após o intervalo, às 16h30, haverá o lançamento do Acervo Carmem Silva digitalizado, organizado pelo Niem/UFRGS. Às 16h45, a terceira mesa, “Das convergências aos compromissos”, reunirá representantes do sistema de justiça, da segurança pública e das políticas para as mulheres para discutir propostas de prevenção e enfrentamento aos feminicídios no estado.
Estão confirmadas Viviane Nery Viegas, secretária adjunta da Secretaria da Mulher do RS; Bibiana Veríssimo, coordenadora do Núcleo de Defesa da Mulher (Nudem) da Defensoria Pública; Luciana Casarotto, promotora de Justiça da 4ª Vara de Feminicídios de Porto Alegre; Télia Negrão, articuladora territorial do Ministério das Mulheres; Natália Fetter, do Conselho Estadual dos Direitos da Mulher; e Daiane Oliveira, da Coordenadoria da Mulher de Nova Santa Rita e da coordenação do Comitê Intermunicipal de Fortalecimento da Rede de Políticas para Mulheres do RS.
A coordenação será de Fabiane Lara dos Santos. Como debatedoras, participam Renata Teixeira Jardim, do Cladem, e Stela Meneghel, da UFRGS e Fiocruz.

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/13.title: 13th-Century Carving Stolen by Art Thief ‘Eric the Belgian’ Recovered in the UK
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/13.author: Lmiller
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/13.text:
Spain’s National Police have spent the past 47 years searching for a Romanesque wood carving of the Virgin Mary that was stolen from the Church of Sa Pedro de Meoz in Navarre, part of the Basque area of northern Spain. At last, they finally found it.
The 21-inch-tall gilded object was nabbed by the notorious “gentleman thief” René Alphonse van den Berghe, known as Erik the Belgian, who robbed churches and monasteries in rural Spain in the late 1970s and early ’80s. Many of his marks have since been recovered. In 2023, for example, a missing fragment from a set of six 17th-century Flemish tapestries was returned to the church in Castrojeriz, Spain, from where Erik the Belgian had swiped them in 1980.
As reported in El País, the investigation leading to this latest discovery picked up steam in April. The authorities knew that Erik the Belgian transported most of his loot from Spain to other European countries “with higher demand in the art and antiques market.”
The local paper Noticias de Navarra notes that in 2012 the Virgin sculpture was sold by a Belgian antique dealer named Bernard Descheemaker, and that by 2017 it was part of the collection Daniel Kanz Gallery in London.
In 2020, according to El País, it found its way to Maastricht in the Netherlands as part of TEFAF, the prestigious art and antiques fair organized by the European Fine Art Foundation. It then “passed through the hands of various antique dealers and collectors,” eventually landing with a Spanish art collection in the UK.
The handover took place at the Spanish Embassy in London, and the piece is now back in Spain.

https://taz.de/Debatte-um-Linken-Abgeord.title: Debatte um Vanessa Emde: Ende für Emde?
https://taz.de/Debatte-um-Linken-Abgeord.author: Jana Laborenz
https://taz.de/Debatte-um-Linken-Abgeord.text:
Debatte um Vanessa Emde: Ende für Emde?
Am Dienstag könnte die Linksfraktion in Berlin die Abgeordnete Vanessa Emde ausschließen. Nicht nur in Berlin ist der Ausschluss umstritten.
Am Dienstag stimmt die Linksfraktion in Berlin über den Ausschluss der umstrittenen Abgeordneten Vanessa Emde ab. Bleibt Emde in der Fraktion, könnte eine rot-grün-rote Regierung in Berlin scheitern. SPD und Grüne haben Emdes Ausschluss zur Bedingung für weitere Gespräche gemacht.
Seit Wochen kreist die Debatte um eine linke Regierung in Berlin um Emde. Die direkt gewählte Abgeordnete aus Neukölln hatte bei der Abgeordnetenhauswahl 46,2 Prozent der Erststimmen geholt. Emde steht wegen ihrer Aussagen zum Nahostkonflikt in der Kritik, sie zeigte sich zudem immer wieder mit dem Aktivisten Ramsis Kilani, den die Partei wegen terrorverherrlichender und teils antisemitischer Aussagen ausgeschlossen hatte. Nach der Wahl unterschrieb Emde ein Papier, in dem sie die Erklärung der Fraktion zu Antisemitismus und Israels Existenzrecht anerkannte – distanzierte sich aber später auf Instagram davon. Beim Landesparteitag der Linken in Berlin protestierte Emde vor der Halle gegen ihre eigene Partei.
Die Berliner Linke erklärte schließlich, sie sehe „keine Arbeitsgrundlage“ mit Emde und forderte sie auf, ihr Mandat niederzulegen. Was diese nicht tat. Vergangene Woche legte der Fraktionsvorstand dann einen Antrag vor, über den die Fraktion diesen Dienstag abstimmen soll. Der Fraktionsvorsitzende der Berliner Linken, Tobias Schulze, sagte der taz: „Frau Emde zeigt bis heute keine Bereitschaft, sich an gemeinsame Beschlüsse der Partei zu halten“. Auch das Existenzrecht Israels gehöre zum Grundsatzprogramm der Partei. Für einen Ausschluss braucht es zwei Drittel der Stimmen. Aus der Partei heißt es, man lasse einen solchen Antrag nur abstimmen, wenn die Mehrheit sicher sei. Die Abstimmung am Dienstag bleibt geheim.
Linke uneinig über Emde
Der Fall Emde ist innerhalb der Linken umstritten. Parteichefin Ines Schwerdtner warf Emde zuletzt eine „Ego-Show“ vor. Auch prominente Mitglieder wie Bundestagsvizepräsident Bodo Ramelow forderten bereits, Emde solle die Fraktion freiwillig verlassen.
Gleichzeitig solidarisieren sich Mitglieder der Linken immer wieder mit Emde. Anfang Oktober forderten 120 Mitglieder in einem offenen Brief, Ausschlussverfahren müssten „sofort enden“. Auch die stellvertretende Parteivorsitzende Özlem Demirel und mehrere Bundestagsabgeordnete unterschrieben, darunter Nicole Gohlke. Diese sagte der taz: Dass Emde gegen die eigene Partei protestierte, habe sie „einiges an Solidarität gekostet – auch bei mir.“ Dennoch hält Gohlke einen Ausschluss weiter für falsch, Emde sei ein „Bauernopfer“ einer rechten Kampagne gegen die Linke.
Auch die Bundestagsabgeordnete Cansın Köktürk unterstützte den Brief. Sie teilte der taz mit: „Ein Ausschluss von Vanessa Emde wird ganz sicher nicht dazu führen, dass Palästina-Solidarität aus der Partei verschwindet. Im Gegenteil: Die Konsequenz wird sein, dass noch mehr palästinasolidarische Menschen eintreten, sich organisieren und innerhalb der Partei für ihre Positionen kämpfen werden.“
Bundespolitischer Druck auch von SPD und Grünen
Auch SPD und Grüne wirken derweil auf ihre Berliner Landesverbände ein. In einem weiteren offenen Brief mehrerer SPD-Größen heißt es: „Unter den gegenwärtigen Voraussetzungen sprechen wir uns mit Nachdruck gegen eine Koalition mit der Berliner Linken aus.“ Unterschrieben hatten auch Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius und Ex-Bundesgesundheitsminister Karl Lauterbach. Auch führende Grünen-Politiker hatten sich bereits zu Wort gemeldet. Während allerdings die Berliner SPD von Anfang an etwas skeptischer gegenüber einer linken Regierung war, sprachen sich die Grünen von Anfang an dafür aus.
Theoretisch wäre auch eine Regierung aus Grüne, SPD und CDU möglich. Die hatte bereits zu Gesprächen eingeladen. Bisher lehnen allerdings SPD und Grüne Sondierungsgespräche ab.

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/fr.title: Friedrich Christian Flick, Art Collector and Scion of German Industrialists with Nazi Past, Dies at 82
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/fr.author: Harrison Jacobs
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/fr.text:
Friedrich Christian Flick, a major collector of contemporary art and scion to one of Germany’s wealthiest industrialist families, died at 82 in Rosenheim in southern Germany. Flick died after suffering injuries from a fall days earlier, according to Monopol magazine.
Flick was a fixture of ARTnews Top 200 Collectors in the early 2000s, appearing on the list consecutively from 1999 to 2007. Flick’s collection is comprised of some 2,500 works, including major pieces by Bruce Nauman, Alberto Giacometti, Marcel Duchamp, Gerhard Richter, Georg Baselitz, Paul McCarthy, and Martin Kippenberger.
His patronage of the arts was not without controversy. His grandfather, Friedrich Flick, who died in 1972, was a top arms supplier to Nazi Germany and had built his company, which included production of coal and steel, on forced labor.
In 2001, Flick hired Rem Koolhaas to design a new museum to house the collection in Zurich. The project was met with protests both from writers and artists, as well as major Jewish groups, who criticized Flick for not contributing to a $6 billion fund for survivors of slave labor factories like those run by his grandfather.
The museum project was abandoned, and in 2003, Flick sought a new path for showing the works from the collection through a partnership with the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, which operates Berlin’s museums. Flick loaned the collection for seven years to Hamburger Bahnhof museum and paid to renovate a 19th-century warehouse into an annex for the museum, as the New York Times reported at the time. According to Monopol, Flick also commissioned the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation to conduct research into his family’s Nazi past, founded a foundation against xenophobia and racism, and donated €5 million to the forced labor fund.
Those moves did little to quell the controversy. In a 2004 op-ed for Handelsblatt, a German business newspaper, Salomon Korn, the vice president of Germany’s Central Council of Jews, called the deal “a kind of whitewashing of blood money into a socially accepted form of art property.” In an open letter, Korn asked further, “Will there soon be a ‘Göring Collection’ in Berlin?”
Per Monopol, Flick later said the response “deeply distressed” him, but that it “forced me to grapple with my family history.” Still, in a 2004 interview with NPR, Flick argued that his family’s Nazi past should not be presented with the works in collection.
“My family history led me to collect works from the kinds of artists who ask irritating questions and challenge people,” he said. “But the family story has to be separated from the presentation of the collection. It would abuse the artwork to present it in the context of my family history. The art is not there for that. It stands on its own.”
The partnership between Flick and the Hamburger Bahnhof continued until 2021, when the halls renovated by Flick to house his art were sold off to a private real estate company, which decided to demolish them. Some of Flick’s works remain on view elsewhere in Berlin: In 2008 and 2014, Flick donated 268 works, including pieces by McCarthy, Pipilotti Rist, Stan Douglas, and others, to the National Gallery. It is not yet clear what will happen to the rest of the collection.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Câmara aprova texto-base do ajuste fiscal com 353 votos a favor e 128 contrários
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A Câmara Federal aprovou nesta terça-feira (23) o texto-base do Projeto de Lei Complementar 299, de 2026, que trata do ajuste fiscal. O projeto foi aprovado por 353 votos favoráveis, ante 128 contra o texto, além de 5 abstenções. Foram rejeitadas todas as emendas apresentadas ao projeto: foram 129 votos a favor das emendas e 319 votos contra as emendas, além de 4 abstenções.
O relator, deputado Mauro Benevides Filho (União Brasil-CE), manteve sem alterações a versão do texto aprovada pelos senadores. Porém, também foram apresentados dez destaques ao projeto. Se eles forem rejeitados, o projeto segue direto para a sanção presidencial. Se forem aprovados, o texto volta ao Senado.
A sessão teve início às 18h, mas o texto-base só foi aprovado mais de 4 horas depois. A oposição de extrema direita tentou obstruir a votação, mas não conseguiu. A deputada federal Júlia Zanatta (PL-SC), líder da oposição, disse que o ajuste fiscal “é tirar dinheiro do povo cobrando mais impostos e tirar dinheiro dos estados congelando o recurso que teria que ser repassado”, e orientou o voto contrário ao PLC 299.
O líder do governo, deputado federal Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS), destacou que o projeto ataca benefícios fiscais injustificados e preserva políticas sociais. E rechaçou as críticas da oposição. “O povo brasileiro sabe que jamais partiria do presidente Lula, um ajuste que prejudicasse o povo brasileiro. Eu acho um absurdo quando colegas parlamentares vêm aqui mentir sobre cortes na saúde e na educação”, afirmou.
Antes da votação, a urgência do projeto foi aprovada com 318 favoráveis, 135 contrários e seis abstenções, o que permitiu votar o projeto diretamente no plenário, sem passar pelas comissões.
O que prevê o projeto
Com a proposta, o governo pretende conter o crescimento das despesas e ampliar a arrecadação para estabilizar a dívida pública. A meta é alcançar um superávit primário de cerca de R$ 18,7 bilhões em 2027.
Entre as principais medidas está a permissão para que o governo bloqueie mais despesas do que exige hoje a Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal (LRF). Nos anos em que isso for necessário para cumprir a meta, o crescimento real dos gastos ficará limitado a 2%, contra os 2,5% permitidos pelo arcabouço fiscal. O texto também efetiva uma defesa antiga do governo: um novo corte linear de 10% nos benefícios fiscais concedidos a diferentes setores da economia.
O relator, Benevides Filho, lembrou que os incentivos fiscais somam cerca de R$ 800 bilhões no país. “Oitocentos bilhões de reais é um valor muito grande. Não existe nenhum outro país que tenha um volume de incentivo fiscal como tem o Brasil hoje”, disse. O relator também negou que o projeto atinja programas como o Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC), o Bolsa Família, o abono salarial e o seguro-desemprego. “Quem falar em corte de benefício social não leu a matéria”, declarou.
Segundo ele, novas medidas poderão ser discutidas depois, em projetos complementares, como a retirada dos investimentos do limite de crescimento dos gastos.
Créditos tributários na mira
Após negociação no Senado, o governo também preservou o dispositivo que autoriza o Executivo a limitar o uso de créditos tributários cruzados para quitar impostos devidos à Receita Federal. Hoje, empresas com créditos podem deixar de pagar outros tributos, ainda que de origem diferente daqueles que geraram o crédito. Entre janeiro e setembro de 2026, as empresas declararam ter usado R$ 200,1 bilhões em créditos para pagar tributos federais, segundo levantamento do g1 com dados da Receita.
Pelo projeto, o governo poderá restringir essas compensações em momentos de contenção de gastos, com percentuais diferenciados de acordo com o valor. Na prática, parte dos tributos que hoje é paga com créditos terá de ser quitada em dinheiro pelas empresas, o que tende a elevar a arrecadação no curto prazo.
Críticas ao projeto
O texto enfrentou diversos questionamentos. Entre os movimentos populares, o dirigente do Movimento dos Trabalhadores Rurais Sem Terra (MST) João Pedro Stedile classificou a proposta como enganação e cobrou que o foco esteja na queda dos juros da dívida.
Em entrevista ao jornal Folha de S. Paulo, publicada na quinta-feira (19), o dirigente defendeu que a estabilização das contas públicas deve priorizar a redução das taxas de juros pagas na rolagem da dívida, a taxação dos super-ricos e a revogação da Lei Kandir, além de cobrar uma renovação geracional com ministros mais jovens para o quarto mandato do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).
“Não entendo por que colocar esta discussão agora na mesa, ainda mais sem uma discussão com as bancadas na Câmara e no Senado da coligação que reelegeu o presidente Lula”, criticou Stedile à Folha.
Para o líder do MST, a investida sobre o ajuste atende a interesses dos setores de maior renda, gerando descontentamento tanto no campo progressista quanto na oposição em razão da indefinição sobre onde incidirão os cortes nas despesas.
Durante a votação, a deputada federal Sâmia Bomfim (Psol-SP) manifestou preocupação com os impactos do projeto para os mais pobres.
“A Faria Lima perdeu nas urnas e agora quer governar pelo orçamento. O presidente Lula tem a força das ruas para resistir a esse assédio e pode contar com a gente nessa briga. Apresentamos propostas concretas para que o ajuste não caia nas costas de quem depende do SUS, da escola pública e do salário mínimo”, disse a parlamentar.
Ela apresentou duas emendas ao projeto: a primeira corta R$ 22,7 bilhões em emendas parlamentares e destina o valor a investimento público; a segunda proíbe o bloqueio de recursos do combate ao feminicídio.
O Partido Liberal (PL) votou contra o projeto de ajuste fiscal. O líder do partido na Câmara, deputado federal Sóstenes Cavalcante (RJ), afirmou que o projeto “não ajusta nada” e mantém “irresponsabilidades” fiscais do governo federal. Ele também acusou o governo de retirar verba da saúde e da educação, ignorando que o projeto do partido na campanha presidencial previa um corte de R$ 200 bi nas áreas sociais.
Em live no sábado (21), Lula rebateu as críticas e garantiu que não haverá cortes nos recursos da saúde e da educação nem redução do salário mínimo. “Não haverá nenhuma hipótese de eu tirar um centavo dos pobres para controlar o orçamento”, afirmou.
Segundo o presidente, parte do ajuste virá da redução de benefícios fiscais a empresas, com impacto estimado em R$ 15 bilhões, sem atingir as pequenas empresas optantes pelo Simples Nacional nem os microempreendedores individuais (MEIs). Outros R$ 18 bilhões devem vir da limitação ao uso de créditos tributários pelas empresas. “Por isso que a Fiesp chiou, por isso que os empresários são contra”, comentou.
Lula também subiu o tom contra o mercado financeiro. “O que eu não posso ficar aceitando é que esse bando de yuppie da Faria Lima fique querendo toda hora questionar a seriedade do governo, como se eles estivessem preocupados com o ajuste fiscal e com os pobres”, criticou.

https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.title: Europe’s big threat is not Trump and Putin redrawing the map. It’s our own learned helplessness | Natalie Tocci
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.author: Nathalie Tocci
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text:
The first ever trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin was rich in symbolism and empty of substance. Many Europeans, filled with anxiety about the Chinese, Russian and US presidents potentially colluding, saw chilling echoes of the Yalta conference in 1945, when Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt redrew the map of Europe.
But those – particularly in eastern Europe – who are fretting about another historic betrayal should remember that when it comes to European security today, we are the ones who hold most of the cards. Far more meaningful last week than Shenzhen was a gathering in Berlin, held at exactly the same time.
True, the Shenzhen summit brought together three autocratic leaders who would like to see the world carved up into spheres of influence, but their meeting turned out to be no Yalta 2.0. The original Yalta took place as the second world war drew to a close, when international law and multilateral organisations were little more than a pipedream. The world was still living in an age of empire, with many colonies in the hands of European countries and the Soviet Union eager to consolidate its own in eastern Europe. It was hardly surprising, back then, that the war’s victors, the US, the UK and the USSR, held the keys to Europe’s future.
Nothing of the kind was ever going to happen in Shenzhen, nor will it at any future gathering of Xi, Trump and Putin alone. Two of the three – Putin and Trump – cannot win the wars they have launched against Ukraine and Iran respectively. The third, Xi, by far the strongest of the trio, is doing little more than bask in the colossal mistakes of his American and Russian friends.
This is not to say that the three are irrelevant to Europe’s security. Russia and the US hold the world’s largest nuclear arsenals. Had Trump, Putin and Xi committed to nuclear arms control, as Trump wanted, Europe (and the rest of the world) would have applauded. But the Russian and Chinese leaders were never going to indulge Trump on that score. Possessing nuclear weapons is the only reason Putin can still claim a seat at the top table; without them, Russia would be little more than a second-rate power. China, meanwhile, in its scramble for superpower status, is racing to expand its nuclear arsenal, and catch up with the US and Russia.
Russia, China and the US also matter in other dimensions of security. Putin’s Russia continues its military assault on Ukraine, which faces its hardest winter since Russia invaded.
