Les cookies et technologies similaires que nous utilisons sur Mediapart sont de différentes natures et nous permettent de poursuivre différentes finalités. 
Certains sont nécessaires au fonctionnement du site et de l’application mobile (vous ne pouvez pas les refuser). D’autres sont optionnels mais contribuent à faciliter votre expérience de lecteur ou de lectrice et d’une certaine façon à soutenir Mediapart. Vous pouvez les refuser ou les accepter ci-dessous, selon leurs finalités. 
Acceptez-vous que Mediapart utilise des cookies ou technologies similaires pour les finalités suivantes ? 
Vous pouvez faire votre choix, pour chaque catégorie, en activant ou désactivant le bouton interrupteur.
                    
                            
                                Nécessaires au fonctionnement
du site ou de l’application
                            Connexion des abonné·es, mesure d’audience anonymisée, envoi des notifications push, suivi des pannes, mise en avant de nos services : ces outils sont nécessaires au suivi de l’activité de nos services et à leur bon fonctionnement.
                                    Voici les différents cookies et technologies similaires compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Cookies d’authentification : connexion des abonné·es.
- Batch (uniquement sur l’application) : envoi de notifications push et de messages in-app.
- Affichage de contenus éditoriaux multimédias : vidéos (YouTube, Dailymotion, Vimeo, INA), réseaux sociaux (Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, Twitter), documents (Scribd, Document Cloud, Slideshare), sons (SoundCloud, Spotify, Deezer), cartes (Google Maps, Mapbox, CartoDB, uMap), infographies (Highcharts, GitHub, Datawrapper, Flourish, Infogram, ThingLink, jQuery, Google Fonts, Bootstrap), live blogs (24liveblog, CoverItLive), aide à l’intégration de média dans les publications Journal et Club (Embedly).
- Datadog (uniquement sur le site web) : indicateurs techniques et équilibrage de charge.
- Firebase Cloud Messaging (uniquement sur l’application) : nécessaire au fonctionnement des notifications push sur Android.
- Microsoft App Center (uniquement sur l’application) : système de mise à jour et de suivi des pannes de l’application.
- Piano : mesure d’audience anonymisée
- Selligent (uniquement sur le site web) : communication avec l’abonné·e, mise en avant des services, offres et avantages.
- Typeform : questionnaires facultatifs pour recueillir les avis des lecteurs sur nos produits numériques.
                                                    
                                            
                            
                            Ces outils nous permettent de recueillir des statistiques de fréquentation du site et de l’application mobile pour comprendre les usages, détecter d’éventuels problèmes et optimiser l’ergonomie de nos produits.
                                    Voici les outils tiers compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Batch (uniquement sur le site web) : mesure d’audience reliée à l’identifiant d’abonné·e.
- CrazyEggs (uniquement sur le site web) : analyse de parcours client.
- Nonli (uniquement sur le site web) : permet à notre équipe des réseaux sociaux de publier les contenus Mediapart sur les réseaux sociaux.
- Piano : mesure d’audience reliée à l’identifiant d’abonné·e.
- Qiota (uniquement sur le site web) : gestion du système de datawall.
                                                    
                                            
                            
                            Il n’y a pas de publicité sur Mediapart. Mais nous faisons la promotion de nos contenus et services sur d’autres sites et réseaux sociaux. Pour cela, nous utilisons les technologies mises à disposition par certains acteurs publicitaires.
                                    Voici les outils tiers compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Facebook (uniquement sur le site web) : ciblage d’audience sur les réseaux sociaux pour faire la promotion de Mediapart.
                                                    
                                            
                            
                                Gestion de l’accès aux contenus
                            Nous utilisons le service Qiota d’Opper Marketing Suite pour configurer l’activation d’un datawall sur certains de nos contenus (uniquement sur le site web). Ce dispositif destiné aux utilisateur·ices non abonné·es requiert la saisie d’une adresse email pour accéder aux contenus concernés. En fournissant cette information, l’utilisateur consent à sa collecte, son stockage et son utilisation à des fins statistiques. Conformément à la réglementation en vigueur, les utilisateurs disposent d’un droit d’accès, de rectification et de suppression de leurs données, qu’ils peuvent exercer en contactant dpo@opper.io.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120414.title: Berlin-Wahl | Vanessa Emde: Der Sturm zieht gerade erst auf
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120414.author: Marten Brehmer
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120414.text:
- Berlin
- Berlin-Wahl
Vanessa Emde: Der Sturm zieht gerade erst auf
Vanessa Emde ist aus der Linksfraktion im Berliner Abgeordnetenhaus ausgeschlossen. Ein Ende des Streits um Nahost dürfte das kaum bedeuten.
Einen Vorgeschmack darauf, wie die nächsten Wochen in der Linken verlaufen werden, konnten Interessierte am Dienstagabend im Veranstaltungsraum »Casino« in Neukölln bekommen. »Der rot-grün-rote Senat soll vor uns zittern«, soll Hannah Bruns dort gesagt haben. Eingeladen hatte der Jugendverband Solid unter dem Titel »Palästina-Solidarität ist kein Verbrechen! Raus aus der Defensive!« Gekommen waren etwa 150 Menschen – nach einer ad-hoc-Umfrage in großer Mehrheit selbst Parteimitglieder.
Dass man den Ausschluss von Vanessa Emde aus der Linksfraktion im Berliner Abgeordnetenhaus nicht verhindern konnte, bezeichnete Bruns als »Klatsche«, die Vorwürfe gegen die Neuköllner Abgeordnete nannte sie eine »Verleumdungskampagne«. Gegen Bruns selbst läuft ein Parteiausschlussverfahren. Sie hatte sich in einem Fernsehinterview explizit nicht vom Terror der Hamas distanziert. Ihrer Motivation scheint der drohende Parteiausschluss wenig geschadet zu haben. »Wir dürfen uns auf keinen Fall ohnmächtig machen«, sagte sie bei der Veranstaltung, wie die »Morgenpost« dokumentierte.
Tatsächlich glaubt niemand in der Linken, dass der Dauerstreit um Nahost mit dem Rauswurf Emdes, den die Linksfraktion am Dienstagnachmittag mit Drei-Viertel-Mehrheit beschloss, enden wird. Schon allein, weil Emde weiter Parteimitglied bleiben wird. Ein Ausschlussverfahren wie bei Bruns ist für Emde nach nd-Informationen nicht geplant. Sie ist auch weiterhin eine der rund 150 Delegierten zum Landesparteitag – auch wenn sie selbst zuletzt vorzog, vor dem Tagungssaal zu demonstrieren, statt sich drin an den Beratungen zu beteiligen.
Nach ihrem Fraktionsausschluss gab sich auch Emde kämpferisch. »Ihr seid nicht allein, wir sind nicht allein – und wir werden uns organisieren«, sagte sie im Abgeordnetenhaus. Emde rief propalästinensische Linke auf, weiter Mitglied der Linkspartei zu bleiben. In zahlreichen Medien war zuletzt spekuliert worden, der radikal palästinasolidarische Flügel der Linken könnte zu der kleinen Partei Mera 25 oder zum BSW übertreten, in denen antizionistische Positionen Parteilinie sind. Hand und Fuß hat das allerdings nicht. Das wäre für die Parteiführung »ein Geschenk«, sagte Linksjugend-Vertreterin Chiara Stenger bei der Veranstaltung in Neukölln.
Auch außerhalb des Jugendverbands gibt es nicht wenige Genossen, die ähnlich ticken wie Emde. »Ihr Ausschluss folgt auf eine wochenlange Kampagne, in der falsche Antisemitismusvorwürfe instrumentalisiert wurden, auch um das palästinasolidarische Profil der Partei zu schwächen«, reagierte der Neuköllner Linke-Bezirksvorsitzende Hermann Nehls auf Emdes Ausschluss aus der Fraktion.
Mit dieser Position steht er nicht allein da. Auch in den Bezirksverbänden Mitte und Tempelhof-Schöneberg gibt es relativ starke Strömungen, die wenig Problematisches daran finden, Israel das Existenzrecht abzusprechen. In der Abgeordnetenhausfraktion stimmten sechs Abgeordnete gegen Emdes Ausschluss, vier enthielten sich. Die prominenteste Fürsprecherin hatte Emde in Vizefraktionschefin Martha Kleedörfer.
Angesichts dieser Lage änderten Fraktions- und Landesspitzen der Partei zuletzt merklich ihre Argumentation. »Die Vorwürfe, dass das Eintreten für eine Ein-Staaten-Lösung per se antisemitisch sei, weisen wir entschieden zurück. Diese Diskussion wird auch in Teilen der israelischen Linken und international geführt«, heißt es in einer Erklärung, die der Fraktionsvorstand nach der Sitzung am Dienstag versandte. Man sei »eine Partei der Palästina-Solidarität«.
Stattdessen stellte man Emdes Verhalten in den Vordergrund. Sie habe sich »jeder konstruktiven Zusammenarbeit in der Fraktion verweigert«. Man habe den Dialog gesucht, sei jedoch auf eine Verweigerungshaltung gestoßen. Die Bundesvorsitzende Ines Schwerdtner warf Emde zuletzt öffentlichkeitswirksam eine »Ego-Show« vor, um sie im nächsten Satz inhaltlich in Schutz zu nehmen. Auch in der Sitzung der Linksfraktion soll Kritik an Emdes Verhalten inhaltliche Fragen überschattet haben, wie Abgeordnete berichten.
Eine »Brücke« nennt ein Fraktionsmitglied das. Denn über die Kritik an Emdes Unzuverlässigkeit habe man sich einfacher einig werden können als über gemeinsame Position zur Nahost-Frage. Auch innerparteilich hofft man, die Wogen so zumindest bis zum Abschluss der Koalitionsverhandlungen glätten zu können.
Ob das gelingt, ist allerdings mehr als zweifelhaft. Die Landesarbeitsgemeinschaft Palästina-Solidarität organisiert in Berlin eine dreistellige Zahl von Mitgliedern, die über Chatgruppen eng vernetzt sind. Die Gruppe könnte das nutzen, um gezielt zu Parteiveranstaltungen und Gremiensitzungen zu mobilisieren. Der Fraktionsausschluss Emdes könnte für die Aktivitäten der Gruppe sogar förderlich sein.
Seit Abschluss des Waffenstillstands in Nahost im Oktober 2025 hat das Thema deutlich an öffentlicher Aufmerksamkeit verloren, auch die Mobilisierung auf der Straße ließ merklich nach. Dass die Palästina-Aktivisten mit Emde nun eine Märtyrerin gefunden haben, könnte ihnen neuen Schub verleihen.
Zugleich dürfte der Ausschluss Emdes kaum ein Ende der Anschuldigungen gegen die Linkspartei bedeuten. »Der Ausschluss von Vanessa Emde aus der Links-Fraktion ist nicht mehr als Symbolik, um die Koalitionsverhandlungen und damit die eigenen Machtperspektiven zu retten«, wird Cerstin Richter-Kotowski, Vorsitzende der Deutsch-Israelischen Gesellschaft Berlin-Brandenburg, in einer Pressemitteilung zitiert. Der Linkspartei gehörten weiter zahlreiche führende Funktionäre an, die »Hass« verbreiteten. Noch weiter ging Stephan Weh, Vorsitzender der Polizeigewerkschaft GdP, der davor warnte, mit einem Senat unter Linke-Führung würden »extrem einsatzbelastende Versammlungslagen mit Hass und Hetze auf unseren Straßen zunehmen«, wie es in einer Pressemitteilung heißt.
Mitglied der Linksfraktion ist Emde nicht mehr, im Landesparlament bleibt sie aber weiter. Während ihr Ausschluss bedeutet, dass sie die Ressourcen der Fraktion nicht mehr nutzen kann und auch in keinen Ausschüssen mehr Mitglied werden kann, hat er für sie auch Vorteile. Zehn Minuten Redezeit stehen fraktionslosen Abgeordneten pro Sitzung zu. Als Mitglied der Linksfraktion war ihr ein Auftritt vor dem Abgeordnetenhausplenum bislang verwehrt geblieben. Zuletzt hatte Emde versucht, sich neben der Palästinafrage auch als kritische Stimme in der Debatte um die Enteignung großer Wohnungskonzerne zu profilieren. Die Linke musste hier im Rahmen der Sondierungen zahlreiche Kompromisse eingehen. Bereits am Donnerstag könnte Emde bei der Sitzung des Abgeordnetenhauses erstmals das Wort ergreifen.
Kein Milliardär im Rücken
Andere Medien haben Konzerne oder Milliardäre im Rücken. Wir haben die nd.Genossenschaft und Leser*innen wie dich. Das macht uns unabhängig und genau das wollen wir bleiben. Aber es heißt auch: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.
Du kannst direkt hier spenden, einmalig oder regelmäßig, damit nd bleibt.

https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.title: Duran Duran was transformed by Andy Taylor’s rock edge – and never quite the same without him
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.author: Alexis Petridis
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.text:
It’s very easy indeed to paint Andy Taylor as the misfit within the world-beating five-man line-up of Duran Duran. The others were fans of glam and Chic: their avowed intention was to form a band that melded the sophisticated disco of the latter with the extravagant style and experimental art-pop of Roxy Music.
Taylor – who had made what he later called “that fateful journey down to Birmingham” from his home on Tyneside after spotting an ad in the Melody Maker – had tastes that tended towards rock music of a more traditional stripe, as evidenced by the artists he covered on his second solo album, 1990’s Dangerous: Thin Lizzy, Bad Company, AC/DC, Montrose.
Happy enough initially to apply the hair dye and make-up that gave Duran Duran their hip post-punk New Romantic image, by the mid-80s he looked like he’d joined the wrong band entirely. In the photos of Duran Duran taken at the Sanremo pop festival in 1985, his bandmates sport the kind of baggy, spendy designer gear common to British pop stars of the era who’ve done exceptionally well for themselves. By contrast, Andy Taylor looks like he could have been parachuted in from a heavy metal band: his hair long, his ripped vest accessorised with scarves, his belt studded, his eyes hidden behind a pair of sunglasses.
Like drummer Roger Taylor, he left Duran Duran the following year: unlike Roger Taylor, he left not because he could no longer stand the pressure of being a global teen idol and fancied a quiet life, but because he’d negotiated a solo deal with a record label that would allow him to pursue his passion for hard rock, in the company of former Sex Pistols guitarist Steve Jones.
And yet, for all he appears in retrospect have stuck out like the proverbial sore thumb, Andy Taylor was absolutely integral to the success of Duran Duran, and not merely because he was by far the most straightforwardly talented musician in the band. As soon as he arrived in Birmingham he set about transforming what one writer called their “rough, undisciplined” blend of electronics, disco-influenced rhythms and punk-y energy into cohesive songs. His leaning towards rock music gave Duran Duran a peculiar commercial edge, particularly in the US, a country that had failed to really take to punk or glam rock, and viewed disco as an aberration best forgotten.
The standard line is that Duran Duran succeeded in the US because of the rise of MTV, which took to their glamorous and expensively made videos early on. But there’s also a compelling argument that Duran Duran became bigger Stateside than any other British pop band of their era in part because Taylor’s distorted guitar – very audible indeed on Girls On Film, or Hungry Like The Wolf, the latter a song on which Taylor translated Nick Rhodes’ synth lines into something more appropriate for guitar – gave traditionally conservative radio programmers something they could understand: at least a hint of traditional rock music, amid the alienating synthesisers and preponderance of slap.
The sales figures were wildly impressive – both 1982’s Rio and its follow-up Seven And The Ragged Tiger went double-platinum in the US – but commercial success wasn’t enough to paper over the obvious fault-lines emerging within the band. Sessions for the latter album were fraught: Andy Taylor subsequently described them as “a laborious plod”, not much helped by his increasing dependence on cocaine; Rhodes tellingly noted that “everybody was pulling and tugging in different directions”.
Duran Duran went on hiatus after completing an arena tour in 1984, its members indulging in side projects. John and Andy Taylor formed The Power Station with vocalist Robert Palmer. Despite a distinctly funky undertow provided by Chic drummer Tony Thompson, their eponymous debut album leaned into the guitarist’s love of Led Zeppelin. Critically pilloried at the time as the height of mid-80s coked-out excess – decades later, it was re-evaluated for precisely the same reason – the album was successful enough to revitalise Palmer’s career: he swiftly left, tapping Andy Taylor to play on his huge solo hit Addicted To Love. Taylor jumped ship from Duran Duran the following year.
Taylor’s solo career never really took off in a comparable manner to that of the band he’d left, although it offered an intriguing index of his influences: he co-produced and wrote an album for Rod Stewart, and worked with British hard rockers Thunder, Reef and The Almighty. Duran Duran went on to have further commercial success, not least with the 1993 single Ordinary World, but they were never quite the same band without him. You could tell as much from the statement the surviving members issued following his death, which praised the “indelible fire and swagger he brought to our music”, suggested he “drove the songs that took [them] around the world”, and hymned the brief early 2000s moment when he rejoined the band, resulting in the album Astronaut and its accompanying hit single Reach Up For The Sunrise: “That time together, both onstage and in the studio, meant a tremendous amount to us all.”
“There’s a massive Andy Taylor-shaped hole in my heart,” added singer Simon Le Bon. “It’ll never close up.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2026/1.title: Photos: Storms and an El Nino-charged king tide batter California’s coast
https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2026/1.text:
In Pictures
Photos: Storms and an El Nino-charged king tide batter California’s coast
Meteorologists have warned that the king tide could pair with high surf to bring historic surges to parts of the state.
California and other parts of the United States West Coast have experienced record-high water levels, causing flooding, destruction and dangerous waves.
On Wednesday, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) announced that the fishing community of Charleston, Oregon, notched its highest-ever coastal water level, roughly 1.12 metres above the mean high water level.
It was as high as 3.4 metres above the mean low water mark.
Other NOAA stations recorded some of their highest water levels on record, including San Diego, Los Angeles and Santa Barbara, all on the southern California coast.
Further north, the L-shaped municipal pier in Pacifica, a city south of San Francisco, crumbled into the surf after a wave as tall as its platform crashed into it.
In a video on social media, bystanders could be heard voicing astonishment at the sight. “Oh my god, it’s gone. Oh my god,” one person said.
The pier had faced multiple closures in recent years, as seawater weakened its concrete structure, but experts say this week’s conditions were more dangerous than normal.
The high coastal water levels were spurred by a combination of factors, including a phenomenon popularly known as king tides.
The term is applied to the highest tides of the year, created when both the sun and the moon are aligned to create a larger-than-normal tidal bulge, pulling the water with their combined gravitational force.
The king tides have been exacerbated by the El Nino weather pattern as well as human-fuelled climate change.
While El Nino is a regular occurrence, this year’s edition is projected to be stronger than normal, according to forecasters, leading to record-warm waters off the Pacific coast. That warming, in turn, helps churn up powerful storms that contribute to waves battering the shoreline.
San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie announced on Wednesday that his city had made it through the worst of this week’s surge with flooding and waves up to 9 metres, but he warned of more king tides to come.
“The last two weeks have been an important reminder to get prepared for the rest of El Nino season. We’re expecting more king tides in December and January,” he wrote on social media. “We need to take these events seriously, prepare ahead of future storms, and stay alert.”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Tarifaço de Trump foi ‘tiro no pé’, impulsionou recorde de exportações do Brasil e custou derrota nos EUA, analisa cientista político
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: José Eduardo Bernardes
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Quando Donald Trump aplicou o aumento da taxa de importação sobre os produtos brasileiros, a previsão de parte do empresariado era de quebra geral na economia. Um ano depois, o resultado não foi o profetizado. As exportações brasileiras bateram recorde em 2025, mesmo com o tarifaço aplicado pelos Estados Unidos. E o maior preço político acabou sendo pago pelo próprio presidente estadunidense.
A avaliação é do cientista político Francisco Fonseca, professor da PUC-SP e da FGV-SP, em entrevista ao Conexão BdF, da Rádio Brasil de Fato, nesta quarta-feira (25). “Pode-se dizer que o tarifaço que o Trump impôs ao Brasil, e possivelmente a outros países também, foi uma espécie de tiro no pé”, afirma.
O primeiro tiro, segundo Fonseca, foi dentro de casa. A inflação e o desemprego subiram, e Trump “levou uma surra eleitoral”. O Partido Democrata conquistou o controle da Câmara e do Senado nas eleições de meio de mandato, em 3 de novembro. “
“Tem a ver também com a guerra no Irã, mas tem a ver com um país que se fechou e tornou tudo mais caro. Foi um protecionismo não inteligente”, resume o professor.
Do lado brasileiro, a sobretaxa acabou empurrando o país para novos mercados. “O tarifaço nos obrigou a ir atrás de novos parceiros, e esses parceiros responderam positivamente”, diz Fonseca. Mais de 40 mercados registraram recorde de compras de produtos brasileiros em 2025, com destaque para Canadá, Índia, Turquia, Paraguai, Uruguai, Suíça, Paquistão e Noruega.
Se lá fora o governo Lula colhe resultados, aqui dentro enfrenta a pressão do mercado financeiro. “O mercado está tentando fazer o governo de refém. Não é que ele pode, ele já está tentando fazer isso”, afirma o professor. Ele chama a disparada do dólar logo depois do segundo turno de “artificial” e compara o momento a um “terceiro turno”.
É nesse cenário que o novo pacote fiscal chega ao Congresso. A expectativa do governo é que o pacote tenha impacto de R$ 50 bilhões a R$ 60 bilhões em 2027, com corte de 20% em incentivos fiscais federais e novas restrições às compensações tributárias, além da revisão dos supersalários.
Para Fonseca, o fato de o pacote ser moderado “é uma derrota do mercado”, que queria congelar o Bolsa Família e o Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC) e desvincular aposentadorias do salário mínimo. O professor também acha que parte da esquerda, inclusive dentro do PT, reagiu “de maneira exagerada”. Para ele, a crítica deixa de lado o principal: o pacote mexe nos créditos e benefícios tributários das empresas e nos privilégios do topo do funcionalismo.
“Ajuste fiscal, de um ponto de vista democrático, é: quem pode pagar mais, paga mais. Ajuste fiscal não é fazer pagar mais os que ganham menos. Não é o Bolsa Família, não são os direitos sociais. Todo país tem que ter relativo equilíbrio das contas, mas não faz sentido querer ajustar as contas em quem ganha menos, nos mais vulneráveis”, defende.
Na lista de alvos estão as pensões integrais pagas a filhas de militares e os penduricalhos do Judiciário. “São camadas que se apropriaram do Estado, muito fortemente incrustadas no Poder Judiciário e nos militares”, diz Fonseca. Ele cita ainda o empresariado que cobra ajuste, mas faz lobby por isenções: “O discurso é que o ajuste fiscal precisa ser aceito, mas não para ele”.
A montagem do novo governo inclui outra disputa: a cadeira deixada por Luís Roberto Barroso no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF). A vaga foi aberta com a saída de Barroso, em outubro de 2025, e segue desocupada desde que o Senado rejeitou, em 29 de abril, a indicação do advogado-geral da União, Jorge Messias.
“O nome de Jorge Messias se inviabilizou completamente. Por sinal, acho que foi um erro do presidente Lula”, avalia Fonseca.
Para o professor, o impasse abre espaço para um terceiro nome, de preferência uma mulher negra. O STF nunca teve uma ministra negra e hoje conta apenas com Cármen Lúcia como mulher na Corte. “O Brasil tem maioria de mulheres e de pretos e pardos, e as instituições não expressam isso, sobretudo o último grau recursal, que é o Supremo”, afirma.
Lula ainda deve indicar mais três ministros até o fim do mandato, segundo Fonseca, e a pressão das ruas e das redes já começou. “Este é o momento que nós chamamos de janela de oportunidade, como nunca, para a indicação de mulheres e, sobretudo, juristas negras. É fundamental para um país que não é um país de brancos, mas tem as suas instituições embranquecidas”, conclui.
Para ouvir e assistir
O jornal Conexão BdF vai ao ar em duas edições, de segunda a sexta-feira: a primeira às 12h e a segunda às 17h, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM na Grande São Paulo, com transmissão simultânea também pelo YouTube do Brasil de Fato.

https://gothamist.com/news/rikers-detain.title: Rikers detainees were routinely strip-searched in violation of policy, monitor finds
https://gothamist.com/news/rikers-detain.author: Ryan Kost
https://gothamist.com/news/rikers-detain.text:
Detainees held in restrictive housing on Rikers Island were routinely strip-searched when leaving and returning to their cells — in violation of the Department of Corrections’ own policy — according to a new report from the federal monitor overseeing reforms at the jail.
The practice was being carried out under a 2023 security memo issued by the department, the monitor, Steve J. Martin, found.
The unit, known as the Rose M. Singer Center Enhanced Supervised Housing, or RESH, holds people accused of serious violence while in custody. In its most restrictive level, detainees spend their out-of-cell time in individual recreation pens or at restraint desks.
Though department policy requires strip searches when a person enters or leaves the unit, the memo, issued in July 2023, went further, instructing correction officers to search detainees whenever they moved between their cells and the dayroom or restraint chairs.
Martin’s team only learned of the memo in October, even though it had been circulating for more than three years, according to the report. Under federal court orders, the department should have consulted the monitor before establishing the policy. The department told the monitor that various leaders had not been aware of the memo, according to the report.
Nicholas Deml, the court-appointed remediation manager tasked with driving reforms in the jails, joined Martin in asking the department to rescind the memo and issue new guidance in line with existing department policy. The department has agreed, according to the report.
Allegations that staff have used strip searches “to intimidate, harass and/or demean” detainees in the unit also come up in the report, along with concerns that some searches included visual body cavity inspections when not necessary or permitted. The correction department’s internal investigation team has opened an inquiry into the unit's use of strip searches, according to the report.
Detainees held in RESH have complained about routine strip searches before, including in written testimony posted on the Board of Correction’s website, which is routinely anonymized.
One person said they would sometimes stay in their cells for days “so that I don’t have to get strip-searched.” Another person described the setting: “You are strip-searched in front of the officers: the officer desk is right there, so there are multiple officers walking by.”
“I understand you have a job to do, but we shouldn’t be strip-searched every single day,” they added. “People aren’t animals.”
Natalie Fiorenzo, a senior corrections specialist with New York County Defender Services, said the finding “was not shocking.” She’s heard from detainees across the island — and in the new Bellevue Hospital medical facility — that they are “getting strip-searched excessively or seemingly randomly.”
The discovery of a memo that department leaders did not know about also fits a familiar pattern, she added. “I do think that there's probably a lot more where that came from, unfortunately,” she said. And while she noted the memo would be rescinded, Fiorenzo was surprised that Martin and Deml did not recommend informing detainees about the correct policy.
The Department of Correction referred a request for comment to the mayor’s office. City Hall spokesperson Sam Raskin said the Mamdani administration remained “committed to working alongside the Remediation Manager and Federal Monitor to deliver the urgent improvements our jail system needs.”
These findings all appear in the latest report filed this week in the long-running federal case over violence in the city’s jails. The more than 400-page report covers the first half of the year and states that the city’s jails remain both dangerous and dysfunctional. The monitor once again used the term “glacial” to describe the pace of change.
At least nine people have died in the Department of Correction's custody this year. After reviewing the circumstances of those deaths, Martin wrote that long-standing security lapses appeared to contribute to many of them. The report describes officers skipping tours or leaving their posts, drugs moving openly through housing units, and detainees exhibiting distressing symptoms for hours before anyone noticed.
The Correction Officers’ Benevolent Association did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Yonah Zeitz, advocacy director at the Katal Center, a reform group, called the searches “just one of many examples of violations that have been recurring over and over and over across many years.” He noted that the jails are now overseen by a federal monitor, a remediation manager, a reformist mayor and commissioner and both the Board of Correction and the State Commission of Correction.
“[They] are all responsible for oversight, yet these types of violations continue to persist,” Zeitz said. “And it's clear that left alone, these violations will continue to happen again and again and again.”
Still, the monitoring team wrote that the arrival of Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s correction commissioner, Stanley Richards, and Deml’s team earlier this year has “altered the dynamics within the agency,” allowing for better cooperation.
A consultant working for Deml has also produced what the monitor described as the first reliable census of staff posts across the department in more than a decade. Martin said the count was critical for figuring out how to properly staff the city’s jails.

https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: Comment | A missed opportunity for a full accounting of cultural cleansing
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: Robert Bevan
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
It is always gratifying to see one’s work referenced—especially 20 years after the fact. The exhibition Heritage in Resistance: Timbuktu to Odessa, at the Cité de l’Architecture et du Patrimoine in Paris (until 3 January 2027), traces attacks on material and intangible culture in conflicts beginning with the dynamiting of the Bamiyan Buddhas in 2001 and ending in Ukraine, Sudan and Gaza.
The vast exhibition spans art, digital re-creations, photography and filmed interviews. It is conceived of as an investigative report organised into sections on erasure, resistance and repair.
A wall text references my 2006 book The Destruction of Memory: Architecture at War, which first set out systematically why such targeting happens. The exhibition credits me with coining the term “cultural cleansing” in respect of the Bosnian War to explain the pattern of heritage erasure that can accompany, or presage, ethnic cleansing and the persecution of populations. It notes that Unesco adopted the term from 2012 to describe “the destruction of World Heritage Sites by terrorist groups”.
Except that book says much more than that. It talked about this same process in other places such as the Israel-occupied West Bank. It examined cultural genocide (like cultural cleansing, this still has no definition in international law) witnessed in instances ranging from the Ottoman Empire and Native American populations to the Holocaust and Tibet. I would now add the experiences of the Uyghurs in China, the Rohingya in Myanmar, the Yazidis in Iraq and the Palestinians in Gaza to that dreadful list. I argue that patterns of heritage destruction can evidence genocidal intent. Other genocides, such as that in Rwanda, did not have a pronounced material culture component.
These are matters that the Cité de l’Architecture et du Patrimoine exhibition unacceptably skirts. As in Germany and the UK (where a talk at London’s Building Centre including Architects for Gaza was cancelled following an intervention by Lawyers for Israel this summer), the French state and its institutions are censoring pro-Palestinian voices.The crucial work of Forensic Architecture in documenting destruction, for example, is not present after a dispute over the group’s use of “the G word”. How can you explain what has happened to Gaza’s cultural heritage unless you are at least prepared to discuss possible intent and patterns of destruction?
As an investigative report, the show obfuscates as much as it reveals. Institutions and governments shield themselves behind the argument that it is up to the courts to determine genocide. They forget the Genocide Convention’s duties of prevention—as litigated in the 2007 International Court of Justice (ICJ) case, Bosnia and Herzegovina v. Serbia and Montenegro, or South Africa’s inclusion of attacks on culture when considering Palestinian “conditions of life” at the ICJ.
There is an impression that heritage destruction in conflicts has got worse over recent decades and that the propaganda impact of destruction is actually exploited by some groups. The jury is out on this. As reflected in the show, however, the international heritage community has had an almost singular focus on actions by terrorist groups, whereas over the past decades (Islamic State and its affiliates aside) it has been the firepower of United Nations State Parties that has been overwhelmingly responsible for the devastation to material history—including but not limited to the United States, Russia, China, Israel and Saudi Arabia. Isis iconoclastically wrecked religious sites in Mosul, but it was the liberating forces that comprehensively flattened the historic city.
Does loot support terrorism?
Looting, too, is problematically covered in the Paris exhibition. This is a serious issue in war zones where security vanishes. But the myth repeated here that the sale of looted artefacts is a meaningful source of terrorist funding “on a par” with resources such as oil is simply unevidenced. (Recovered Isis documents show something quite different.)
The exhibition is sponsored in part by the French office of Unesco. No surprise then that the organisation’s manifest failure to protect heritage in conflicts is absent from the walls. Unesco is celebrated—as it should be in some cases—for its work in Timbuktu, where the International Criminal Court brought the first (and, to date, only) successful prosecution for the targeting of monuments as a war crime. Less convincingly, the show argues that this episode was a turning point after which Unesco formulated a more grassroots approach to preserving culture by working with local people on local priorities.
It was Unesco that disgracefully praised Putin for liberating Palmyra despite the terrible damage Russian forces allied with Assad inflicted on Syria’s people and heritage. Unesco has been just as partial since: while it “strongly condemns” Russian attacks on heritage in Ukraine and Israel’s on Lebanon, it does not offer the same degree of pressure in its statements on heritage destruction in Gaza or Iran. Even then, unlike other UN agencies, Unesco never names Israel. Unesco has not invoked the 1954 Hague Convention in relation to Gaza, despite citing it in virtually all similar instances. Unesco did not seek urgent action by the UN Security Council or the General Assembly to protect cultural sites there as it did in respect of Isis.
The Paris show is more subtle in its understanding of the ways that post-war heritage reconstruction can be problematic and not necessarily healing, but is just as silent on Unesco’s move away from the centrality of authenticity to reconstruction work. Whereas the notion of rebuilding the Bamiyan Buddhas was deemed unacceptable, Unesco promoted building a brand-new Mostar Bridge in Bosnia and Herzegovina as peacebuilding—despite community relations actually deteriorating in the city. And then the agency had the temerity to declare the facsimile bridge a World Heritage Site, undermining its own scientific tenets to bolster a failed symbolic gesture. All this bad-faith is set out in my follow-up book, Monumental Lies (2022).
One is left to read between the lines for hints at the full curatorial mindset. Once through the exhibition doors, the first large-scale works displayed are photographs by the Palestinian artist Taysir Batniji of Gazans’ retrieved housekeys, with their heartbreakingly quotidian fobs—a friendship bracelet, a cheap carabiner clip, a Minnie Mouse figure. The unknown fate of their owners is pencilled in below.
In its silences and voids, Heritage in Resistance at least accurately mirrors failures of international institutions and laws and the partiality and misinformation that surrounds responses to contemporary heritage destruction. Ultimately, the show offers false hope about successful resistance via digital surveying, reconstruction and Unesco work. What we should be feeling is despair.
- Heritage in Resistance: Timbuktu to Odessa, until 3 January 2027, Cité de l’Architecture et du Patrimoine, Paris
- Robert Bevan is a journalist, author and heritage consultant

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/ta.title: Tate Liverpool Plans Fall 2027 Reopening With Surrealism Survey
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/ta.author: Hikmat Mohammed
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/ta.text:
Tate Liverpool will reopen in fall 2027 after a £30 million transformation with the exhibition “Surrealism: Staging Dream Worlds,” a nod to the museum’s inaugural Surrealist show in 1988.
The surrealism exhibition will run from fall 2027 to spring 2028 and include works by Salvador Dalí, Eileen Agar and Man Ray. According to Tate Liverpool, the show will also explore the “important role of surrealism in the history of theater and dance” through the movement’s major commissions for stage sets and costumes. Also on view will be Dorothea Tanning’s costume designs for the ballet The Witch, photographs of Sheila Legge performing as the “Surrealist Phantom of Sex Appeal” at the opening of the 1936 International Surrealist Exhibition in London, and material from the archive of Ted Joans.
“Surrealism invites us to see the world differently and what better way to reopen Tate Liverpool. This exhibition will spark imaginations, surprise visitors and reward curiosity, offering a fresh perspective on one of art’s most celebrated movements. It also brings a wonderful echo of the surrealist exhibition that opened our gallery in 1988, while taking visitors on an exciting new journey,” said Jemima Pyne, interim director of the Tate Liverpool, in a statement.
Tate Liverpool closed in October 2023 and was scheduled to reopen in 2025, but fundraising difficulties pushed the date back to 2027. The architecture firm 6a architects is redesigning the gallery’s home, an 1846 warehouse on the Royal Albert Dock, as part of a £35 million ($46.5 million) renovation.

https://taz.de/Filmdebuet-Barrio-Triste-.title: Filmdebüt „Barrio Triste“: Aliens in Medellín
https://taz.de/Filmdebuet-Barrio-Triste-.author: Benjamin Moldenhauer
https://taz.de/Filmdebuet-Barrio-Triste-.text:
Filmdebüt „Barrio Triste“: Aliens in Medellín
In seinem Spielfilmdebüt „Barrio Triste“ erzählt der Regisseur Stillz von kolumbianischen Jugendlichen. Von deren Elend aus driftet er ins Irreale ab.
Vier junge Männer in einem Elendsviertel der kolumbianischen Stadt Medellín. Gleich zu Beginn hauen sie einem TV-Reporter aufs Maul und klauen seine Videokamera. Um von da an ihr eigenes Leben in ihrem Viertel zu dokumentieren. Also Alkohol, Arbeitslosigkeit, Dreck, Verrohung und Gewalt. Die groben Kamerabilder zeigen an, dass wir uns in den Achtzigern befinden, vor der Zeit der digitalen Bilder.
„Barrio Triste“, das Debüt des kolumbianisch-amerikanischen Regisseurs und Fotografen Stillz, beginnt wie ein sozialrealistisches Drama im Found-Footage-Modus. Produziert hat den Film der Regisseur Harmony Korine, dessen „Trash Humpers“ eventuell ein Orientierungspunkt für diese filmische Unternehmung war. Der Ton schwankt, die Bilder sind verwackelt, wenn es regnet, gibt es Tropfen auf dem Objektiv und damit auch im Bild.
Am Anfang deutet sich noch so etwas wie ein Plot an. Die Clique raubt ein Juweliergeschäft aus und erschießt einen der Angestellten, es entsteht ein Konflikt und damit so etwas wie eine Geschichte. Die bricht dann aber auch gleich wieder ab, der Film montiert in der Folge Alltagsszenen aus der traurigen Nachbarschaft mit Interviews: eine Schlägerei, ein Besäufnis vor einem brennenden Auto, eine Punkband, die in einer Ruine spielt.
Der Film
„Barrio Triste“. Regie: Stillz. Mit Juan Pablo Baena, Samuel Velásquez u. a. Kolumbien/USA 2026, 89 Min.
Dazu kommen als Ruhepole Interviews, in denen die vier muskulösen, auf der Straße kurz vorm Ausrasten stehenden jungen Männer über ihr Innenleben erzählen. Also darüber, was Tod, Trauer und Glück (Letzteres sei für ihn in dieser Welt nicht vorgesehen, bemerkt einer der vier ganz richtig) für sie bedeuten.
Der Film meint alles todernst
Das alles könnte auf einen fiesen Sozialelendsporno hinauslaufen. „Barrio Triste“ aber nimmt schnell eine andere Abbiegung: Sozialrealismus trifft „The Blair Witch Project“. Stillz’ Film ist, darin dem mit anderen filmästhetischen Mitteln operierenden Elendsviertel-Film „City of God“ ähnlich, aufgeladen und überhitzt.
Dieser Eindruck entsteht hier nicht durch Geschwindigkeit, sondern durch ein immer stärkeres Abdriften ins Irreale, das der Realität dieser Welt auf eine seltsame, befremdliche Weise sehr gerecht wird. Dafür sorgt ganz wesentlich der Score der venezolanischen Produzent*in Arca: hauntologische Elektronik, die antike Synthiesounds mit dem Industrial der Achtziger verbindet, unterschwellig überspannter Noise, Geistermusik.
Was zuerst wie radikaler Sozialrealismus wirkt, schraubt sich gegen Ende hin in ein filmisches Delir. Schon in der ersten Szene wird von Lichtern am Himmel berichtet, die auf Aliens deuten. Am Ende kippt „Barrio Triste“ dann in die Fantastik, hält aber durchgehend an der minimalistischen Found-Footage-Ästhetik fest. Das ist mehr als nur Spielerei, „Barrio Triste“ meint das alles todernst. Was man zu sehen bekommt, die Ausweidung junger Menschen, ist ein einfaches, aber genaues Bild für das, was real passiert in sozialen Welten, in denen die soziale Verelendung herrscht.
Etwas wirkliche Neues schaffen
Stillz hat bereits mit seinem Clip für Bad Bunnys Song „Baticano“ gezeigt, dass er gerne filmhistorische Ästhetiken reproduziert. Da schickte er den Sänger in Nosferatu-Verkleidung durch eine formvollendet expressionistische Schwarz-Weiß-Szenerie und brachte so puertoricanischen Latin-Trap-Reggaeton in Verbindung mit dem Kino der Weimarer Republik.
Empfohlener externer Inhalt
Wir würden Ihnen hier gerne einen externen Inhalt zeigen. Sie entscheiden, ob Sie dieses Element auch sehen wollen:
Trailer „Barrio Triste“
Ich bin damit einverstanden, dass mir externe Inhalte angezeigt werden. Damit können personenbezogene Daten an Drittplattformen übermittelt werden. Mehr dazu in unserer Datenschutzerklärung
Das wirkte noch wie eine Übung, wie postmodernes Zitieren. In „Barrio Triste“ schafft die Verbindung nicht nur zweier Genres, sondern von verschiedenen filmischen Registern etwas wirklich Neues. Etwas Neues, das dann auch nichts mehr mit magischem Realismus zu tun hat. Eben weil hier nichts poetisch verklärt wird.
Musik und VCR-Bilder schließen an die Nostalgieästhetik der 2010er-Jahre an, an den Achtzigerjahre-Retro von „Stranger Things“ bis zur Musik von Oneohtrix Point Never. Um sie dann in eine soziale Hölle zu werfen, die der Retromania alles wehmütig Angenehme nimmt. Und sie stattdessen in ein hitziges filmisches Experiment überführt.

https://www.humanite.fr/monde/benyamin-n.title: En Israël, Eizenkot poursuit ses discussions avec Netanyahou : le gouvernement toujours introuvable

Chargé par le président israélien de former un gouvernement, le chef de l’opposition Gadi Eizenkot multiplie les pourparlers, y compris avec le Likoud de Netanyahou, au risque de s’aliéner ses alliés. Les partis judéo-arabes, objets de menaces et d’invectives quotidiennes, sont prêts à un soutien sans participation pour débarrasser le pays du premier ministre sortant. Le temps presse.
Près d’un mois après les élections législatives du 27 octobre, le chef de l’opposition, Gadi Eizenkot, arrivé en tête du scrutin avec son parti Yashar, n’est toujours pas parvenu à former un gouvernement. Le temps presse : son mandat confié par le président israélien Isaac Herzog prend fin le 6 décembre – il peut être prolongé de quatorze jours.
Une course contre la montre qui révèle l’équation insoluble d’Eizenkot, tiraillé entre une alliance avec les formations de gauche judéo-arabes, la Liste unifiée, où figure...

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120413.title: Ukraine-Krieg | Russischer Botschafter: Erst Moskau, dann Verhandlungen
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120413.author: Antoine Lambroschini
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120413.text:
- Politik
- Ukraine-Krieg
Russischer Botschafter: Erst Moskau, dann Verhandlungen
Offiziell signalisieren Russland und die EU Verhandlungsbereitschaft zum Ukraine-Krieg. Bevor es dazu kommt, stellt Moskau eine neue Bedingung.
Der russische Botschafter in Deutschland hat die Europäer aufgefordert, vor einer Beteiligung an den Verhandlungen über ein Ende des Ukraine-Krieges zu Gesprächen nach Moskau zu kommen. Russland wolle erst ihre »genauen Absichten« in dem Konflikt kennenlernen, sagte Sergej Netschajew in einem am Mittwoch veröffentlichten Interview mit der Nachrichtenagentur AFP. Auf eine entsprechende Einladung des russischen Präsidenten Wladimir Putin hätten die Europäer aber »mit Zurückhaltung« reagiert. Weiter warf der Diplomat Europa vor, keinen Frieden zu wollen, und prangerte eine zunehmende »Militarisierung« Deutschlands an.
Die Europäer fordern seit Langem, an den Gesprächen der USA und der Ukraine mit Russland über den Ukraine-Krieg und europäische Sicherheitsfragen beteiligt zu werden. Sie werfen US-Präsident Donald Trump und Kreml-Chef Putin vor, über ihre Köpfe hinweg Entscheidungen zur sicherheitspolitischen Zukunft Europas treffen zu wollen. Auch an der jüngsten Runde am 10. und 11. November in Abu Dhabi war Europa nur an der Seitenlinie vertreten.
Botschafter: US-Bemühungen sind »ehrlich«
»Wir haben, wie mir scheint, aus Brüssel gehört, dass die Europäer nicht die Absicht haben, nach Moskau zu reisen«, sagte der russische Botschafter im AFP-Interview. »Was uns betrifft, so sind wir zumindest im trilateralen Format Russland-Ukraine-USA bereit, den Dialog fortzusetzen.« Die Bemühungen Trumps und von dessen Unterhändlern Jared Kushner und Steve Witkoff zur Lösung des Konflikts würdigte er als »ehrlich«. Auf europäischer Seite sei hingegen »nichts Vergleichbares« festzustellen.
Die Europäer sollten »natürlich« an Gesprächen über die europäische Sicherheit beteiligt werden, versicherte Netschajew. »Aber wir müssen verstehen, was sie wollen. Und bisher verstehen wir das nicht.« Der Botschafter hob mit Blick auf die Europäer hervor: »Sagt uns, ob ihr eine friedliche Lösung wollt. Im Moment sind wir uns dessen nicht sicher.«
Merz: Europäer sind »selbstverständlich« bereit zu Gesprächen
Putin hatte in der vergangenen Woche nach einem Dreiergipfel mit Trump und Chinas Staatschef Xi Jinping im chinesischen Shenzhen erklärt, er habe die Europäer zu Sondierungsgesprächen nach Moskau eingeladen. Erst danach werde entschieden, »in welchem Format die Gespräche fortgesetzt werden«.
Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) betonte, die Europäer seien »selbstverständlich zu Gesprächen mit Russland bereit«. Bei einem parallel zum Dreiergipfel in Shenzhen abgehaltenen Ukraine-Gipfel in Berlin stellte er in Aussicht, dass diese »nun auch bald stattfinden« würden. Es werde jedoch nach einem Verhandlungsort »auf neutralem Boden« gesucht. Als möglichen Ort nannte der Kanzler die Vereinigten Arabischen Emirate.
Russland hat die Ukraine im Februar 2022 angegriffen und führt nun seit fast fünf Jahren Krieg gegen das Land. Auch in dieser Woche wurde die Ukraine fast jede Nacht von Raketen- und Drohnenangriffen überzogen, es gab mehrere Tote.
Moskau beharrt auf seinen Forderungen
In den bisherigen Verhandlungen hat Moskau keine Zugeständnisse erkennen lassen: Der Kreml beharrt unter anderem auf seiner Maximalforderung, dass die Ukraine den Donbass im Osten des Landes komplett abtreten soll – was Kiew strikt ablehnt.
Eine künftige Sicherheitsarchitektur in Europa müsse auch den russischen »Anliegen Rechnung tragen«, forderte Netschajew. Russland dringt auf eine sicherheitspolitische Neuordnung Europas und lehnt eine Nato-Mitgliedschaft der Ukraine ab. Zudem erachtet Moskau eine mögliche Stationierung westlicher Truppen in der Ukraine nach einem Kriegsende als Bedrohung der eigenen Sicherheit.
Im AFP-Interview verwies der russische Botschafter mit Blick auf die Verhandlungen zum Kriegsende auf einen »Kompromiss«, der auf dem Tisch gelegen habe und bereits bei einem Treffen zwischen Trump und Putin im US-Bundesstaat Alaska bestätigt worden sei. Worin dieser Kompromiss konkret bestehen soll, führte Netschajew nicht aus. Trump hatte Putin im August 2025 in Alaska empfangen. Das Treffen war im Westen auf Kritik gestoßen.
Botschafter sieht keine deutsche Dialogbereitschaft
Mit Blick auf die Beziehungen zu Deutschland äußerte sich Netschajew kritisch. »Leider hören wir in Berlin, dass sie derzeit nicht mit Moskau in Dialog treten wollen«, sagte er. Neben »kriegerischen Erklärungen« vonseiten Berlins seien fünf russische Generalkonsulate sowie das russische Kulturinstitut geschlossen worden.
Die Bundesregierung hatte Russland Anfang September für einen versuchten Sprengstoffanschlag am Leipziger Flughafen verantwortlich gemacht und Sanktionen gegen Moskau verhängt. Sie ordnete unter anderem an, das letzte noch offene russische Generalkonsulat in Bonn zu schließen und den Vertrag mit dem »Russischen Haus« in Berlin zu kündigen.
Kritik an Militarisierung Deutschlands
Im AFP-Interview kritisierte der russische Botschafter zudem die aus seiner Sicht voranschreitende »Militarisierung« Deutschlands. Als Beispiele nannte er die von Bundeskanzler Merz angekündigte Stärkung der Bundeswehr sowie die Stationierung einer deutschen Brigade in Litauen.
Wenn es zu einem Konflikt käme, würde sich diese »Brigade nicht lange halten«, betonte der Botschafter, der zugleich versicherte, dass Russland keinen Angriff plane. »Wir betonen, dass wir auf keinen Fall Krieg gegen Europa oder die Nato führen wollen.«
Mit Blick auf die deutsche Innenpolitik betonte Netschajew, Moskau unterhalte »keinerlei privilegierte Beziehungen« zu einzelnen Parteien. Bestimmte Positionen von AfD und BSW zu einer Wiederannäherung an Russland bezeichnete er jedoch als »vollkommen akzeptabel«. Zu Bundeskanzler Merz wollte er sich nicht äußern. Darüber werde die deutsche Bevölkerung »bei den nächsten Wahlen oder zu einem anderen Zeitpunkt urteilen«. AFP/nd
Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf
Bei uns muss niemand zahlen, um informiert zu sein. Klingt nach einem schlechten Geschäftsmodell? Ist es auch. Aber uns sind unabhängiger Journalismus und Teilhabe für alle wichtiger als Profit. Journalismus kostet trotzdem Geld: Recherche, Druck und all die Menschen, die ihn machen. Deshalb sind wir auf dich angewiesen. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.
Spende einmalig oder regelmäßig, jeder Betrag zählt. Damit nd bleibt.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.title: Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports
https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.author: Mera Aladam
https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.text:
Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports
Fresh explosions rocked Riyadh on Wednesday as Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, as the kingdom’s deterrence and defensive capabilities continue to be challenged.
The Houthis said that both strikes on the ports “resulted in damage” while the Saudi-led coalition acknowledged that a projectile hit the port of Jazan, resulting in minor damage and no casualties.
The port strikes followed an attack on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia’s largest refinery. Argus Media, which covers commodity markets, said the Houthis landed two successful blows on the facility, one at the refinery and one at the export terminal. The Houthis say they bombed Ras Tanura as retaliation for the Saudi attack on the port of Hodeidah controlled by the group.
Saudi Arabia is shooting down the majority of Houthi missiles and drones fired at it, Arab and Western officials tell Middle East Eye, but it has failed to protect key assets like energy facilities, financial centres and airports.

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Pochettino claims officials ‘punished’ Manchester United in chaotic Sporting draw
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Jamie Jackson at the Estádio José Alvalade
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
Mauricio Pochettino claimed Manchester United were punished unfairly after again appearing to suffer from faulty officiating in Wednesday night’s 2-2 draw at Sporting.
The key decision from Szymon Marciniak came when Amad Diallo’s first-half strike was ruled out due to the referee adjudging Youri Tielemans to have fouled Gonçalo Inácio just before the finish. Tielemans was booked and so when he received a second yellow card in second-half added time, he was sent off for United’s fifth red card in their last nine games. This followed Leny Yoro’s red card in Sunday’s 4-0 loss at Liverpool that was later rescinded.
“It’s difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions,” said Pochettino, who greeted questions about the official’s first caution of Tielemans by saying: “It’s difficult to understand why that happened on the field. Impossible.”
With 10 minutes left United were 2-1 ahead but suffered a chaotic ending as Senne Lammens dropped a high cross in front of his goal, allowing Luis Suárez to equalise with a bicycle kick.
Pochettino defended his No 1. “Football is about making mistakes. I want to support always my player. It’s something that happened in that case. We need to talk about responsibility and it’s our responsibility too to provide the best tools,” said the head coach.
“In this type of action also our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult. It’s not to blame the defensive line, but it’s two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. Because sometimes we talk about that professional players need to have refreshed concepts, details until that becomes a habit. And things that we need to improve are habits in a defensive way, offensive way, in all the areas.
“But of course, we need to accept, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve, you know, the small details that for sure we will improve.” Lammens saved a first-half penalty from Suárez before conceding another one himself moments later, which the striker coverted.
Bruno Fernandes equalised from the spot on 48 minutes before his bizarre long-range effort – which took a huge deflection off a divot in the pitch – put United ahead.
Despite the chaotic end, Pochettino was impressed by his team. “The structure was really good,” he said. “All the microdoses that we add to the team, I think is helping the structure to be very clear.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Ukraine attacks Russian military base, says five planes struck
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Ukraine attacks Russian military base, says five planes struck
The Ukrainian General Staff says its forces struck an airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region east of Moscow.
Ukrainian forces have hit a major Russian military base east of Moscow, damaging five aircraft used to launch missiles and bombs, according to the Ukrainian General Staff.
Ukraine struck the Savasleyka airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region, the General Staff said on Wednesday, adding that three MiG-31 jets were used to fire hypersonic missiles and two Su-34 fighter-bombers were damaged.
Russia did not immediately comment on the report by the General Staff, which said the Savasleyka airbase had been hit in the latest long-range attacks aimed at crippling Moscow’s war effort.
The operation followed a series of high-profile strikes by Ukrainian forces in recent days in which two Russian ships were hit in Libyan waters and a Russian vessel was struck in the Gulf of Finland.
Last week, Ukraine destroyed the road portion of Russia’s prized bridge to the Crimea peninsula after consecutive attacks.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and fighting has continued despite a renewed US-backed push to end what has become Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.
Kyiv is trying to dent Moscow’s military might as it struggles under a renewed campaign of attacks on its energy system and mounting Russian strikes on front-line cities.
Ukrainian forces are hunting Russian ballistic-missile launchers used to carry out many of those attacks, striking 16 over the past several months, Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said this week.
Renewed Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian oil refineries’ processing volumes by 45 percent since late October, industry sources said this month. Kyiv has said it will stop striking Russian energy targets only when Moscow does the same.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Alckmin relaciona crescimento das exportações ao fortalecimento do cooperativismo
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Kennedy Cruz
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O vice-presidente da República, Geraldo Alckmin (PSB), defendeu a ampliação da participação de cooperativas e pequenos negócios nas exportações brasileiras durante a abertura do encontro nacional de cooperativas atendidas pelos programas Cooperar para Exportar, Exporta Mais Brasil Cooperativas 2026 e Peiex (de qualificação para a exportação), nesta quarta-feira (25), em Brasília. Ao citar o recorde de US$ 349 bilhões em vendas externas registrado em 2025, ele afirmou que o país deve repetir o resultado neste ano e destacou o cooperativismo como instrumento para ampliar o acesso de pequenos produtores ao mercado internacional.
“No ano passado, mesmo com o tarifaço, batemos recorde de exportações, com US$ 349 bilhões. Neste ano, devemos alcançar um novo recorde, conquistar mercados e ampliar a participação do cooperativismo. A cooperativa dá força. Quanto mais abelhas, mais mel. Ela permite ganhar escala, agregar valor, melhorar a renda e acessar novos mercados”, afirmou.
Entre as iniciativas mencionadas por Alckmin está o programa Acredita Exportação, que prevê a devolução de 3% do valor exportado por micro e pequenas empresas, na forma de crédito tributário, para compensar impostos acumulados ao longo da cadeia produtiva. “As pequenas empresas, quando exportam, recebem do governo 3% do valor exportado para compensar os créditos tributários. Isso dá mais competitividade aos pequenos e permite que as micro e pequenas empresas tenham melhores condições de exportar”, explicou o vice-presidente.
O presidente da Agência Brasileira de Promoção de Exportações e Investimentos (ApexBrasil), Laudemir Müller, também defendeu a ampliação da presença de pequenos produtores no comércio exterior. Para ele, a organização coletiva é uma das principais formas de permitir que agricultores familiares, povos e comunidades tradicionais e extrativistas aproveitem as oportunidades de exportação.
“O Brasil está crescendo e será a oitava economia do mundo. Queremos que essa oportunidade também chegue aos pequenos, à agricultura familiar, aos povos e comunidades tradicionais, aos ribeirinhos e aos extrativistas. A forma de os pequenos aproveitarem as oportunidades do mercado internacional é por meio das cooperativas”, afirmou. “Por isso apoiamos de forma tão intensa o cooperativismo. É por meio das cooperativas que conseguimos chegar ao mercado internacional, exportar nossos produtos e gerar renda para milhares de cooperados em todo o Brasil”, completou o presidente da ApexBrasil.
Desburocratização e redução de custos
Alckmin destacou medidas para simplificar os procedimentos de comércio exterior. Entre elas, citou o Portal Único, ferramenta que reúne etapas dos processos de exportação e importação. Segundo o vice-presidente, a iniciativa deve reduzir o prazo médio de exportação de 13 para cinco dias e o de importação de 17 para seis dias e meio.
Outra medida mencionada foi a Licença Flex, que permite utilizar uma mesma licença em diferentes operações de exportação ou importação por um período de três ou quatro anos, em vez de emitir um documento para cada operação.
O vice-presidente afirmou que a mudança pode reduzir custos para empresas e cooperativas que exportam com frequência. “Imagine uma empresa ou cooperativa que precisa fazer três exportações por semana. Antes, precisava de três licenças, uma para cada operação. Agora, com a Licença Flex, passa a ter uma licença com validade de três ou quatro anos. Isso reduz custos e desburocratiza. Uma carga parada no porto por um dia perde 0,8% do valor da carne. Por isso, é fundamental reduzir o tempo e os custos das operações”, afirmou Alckmin.
Alckmin destacou, ainda, a ampliação dos acordos comerciais do Mercosul, com destaque para as negociações com a União Europeia. Segundo ele, a abertura de novos mercados cria oportunidades para os produtos brasileiros. “Temos o acordo Mercosul-EFTA, que reúne quatro países com algumas das maiores rendas per capita do mundo: Noruega, Suíça, Liechtenstein e Islândia. E, por último, o acordo entre Mercosul e União Europeia, o maior entre blocos econômicos do mundo. De fevereiro para cá, quando entrou em vigor o acordo, nossas exportações para a Europa aumentaram 21%”, destacou.

https://gothamist.com/news/brooklyn-envi.title: Brooklyn environmentalists sue to block Greenpoint waterfront development
https://gothamist.com/news/brooklyn-envi.author: Willow Higgins
https://gothamist.com/news/brooklyn-envi.text:
Environmental activists are suing New York City to stop plans for a waterfront residential complex of more than 1,300 units in Greenpoint that they say sits in a floodplain and will endanger residents.
Friends of Bushwick Inlet Park, a nonprofit that advocates for a public park on the North Brooklyn waterfront, and local environmental activists say in court papers that the city’s environmental review of the Monitor Point project relies on outdated climate projections.
The lawsuit is the latest chapter in a decadeslong disagreement over how the land near the East River’s Bushwick Inlet should be used. A sweeping zoning change in 2005 made way for skyscrapers across swaths of Williamsburg and Greenpoint, but also promised public parkland on the nearly 30 acres surrounding the inlet — heavily polluted land that was historically home to fossil fuel companies. More than 20 years later, according to Friends of Bushwick Inlet Park, only a third of the promised parkland is open.
“Using public land and funding to put people in harm’s way without a thorough, science-based environmental review is just reckless,” said Ari Feldman, a spokesperson for Legal Services NYC, which filed the lawsuit, in a statement. “This project would place hundreds of affordable housing residents, including seniors, in a high-risk floodplain without adequate protections.”
The City’s legal department has yet to file a response to the petition, but told Gothamist it stands by its decision to approve the project.
“We are reviewing the suit and are confident in the integrity of the City's environmental review,” said Nicholas Paolucci, the director of public affairs in the city’s law department, in a statement. “We will be responding further in the litigation.”
Monitor Point, set to be built right next to a narrow edge of the parkland, includes two predominantly market-rate residential towers up to 640 feet tall and a third building intended to be entirely income-restricted. Part of the project will be built on land owned by the MTA, which has agreed to lease its property to the real estate developer Gotham Organization.
The Article 78 petition — a legal filing that challenges the decisions of government agencies — which was filed against New York City, the Department of City Planning, the City Council, the MTA, Gotham Organization and other city agencies, argues that the proposal should not have been approved.
The review process “downplayed and ignored the true costs and climate risks of a project that will deepen the climate dangers for the surrounding community and endanger the fragile Inlet ecosystem, the neighborhood, the Project’s own residents, and people who already reside, work or recreate nearby,” the lawsuit states.
The properties at 40 and 56 Quay Street were rezoned again this summer to make way for the development. In doing so, the environmental review process, according to the lawsuit, relied on outdated climate and flood projections from 2015 that do not include what’s called “compound flooding,” the combination of heavy rainfall with other flood sources like rising groundwater runoff, river levels and storm surges. Doing so “severely underestimated flood risk,” according to the lawsuit.
The New York Panel on Climate Change released new metrics in 2024 that do consider the risks of compound flooding, and, according to the lawsuit, those updated metrics should be incorporated into the city’s environmental review process.
Opponents of the project said that the area where Monitor Point is planned has flooded before. Hurricane Sandy left it 12 feet underwater, according to the lawsuit, noting that risks from climate change have since increased.
Katherine Conkling Thompson, president of Friends of Bushwick Inlet Park and one of the Article 78 petitioners, told Gothamist she is particularly concerned about flooding risks because the Monitor Point proposal touts 662 affordable units, including more than 160 deeply affordable units for seniors and 110 for formerly homeless New Yorkers.
“The city would be investing… hundreds of millions of dollars in housing for particularly at-risk people,” Thompson said. “These are formerly unhoused people and elderly… in a very flood-prone location. We think that’s unwise and needs more scrutiny.”
Ron Shiffman, a city planner and professor emeritus at the Pratt Institute, filed an affidavit supporting the lawsuit against the city agencies. More affordable housing in New York is paramount, he argued to the court, but it should also be done right.
“New York urgently needs more housing, and especially more housing affordable to very low, low- and moderate-income households,” Shiffman stated in the legal filing. “But affordable housing production cannot be treated as a substitute for planning and community development.”

https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: Smithsonian leader defends institution's independence after leak of White House’s draft overhaul plan
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: Elena Goukassian
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
Lonnie G. Bunch III, the outgoing leader of the Smithsonian Institution, sent a letter to staff on Tuesday (24 November) in an attempt to quell fears of a political takeover after photos leaked of a Trump aide working on an overhaul plan while riding the city's metro.
“The intended use of this list is unclear,” Bunch wrote of “The Smithsonian Institution Renewal Plan” that the staffer was seen editing on his laptop on a crowded train in late October. “What remains clear is that the Smithsonian is an independent institution with the responsibility and privilege to present accurate information to millions of visitors through our scholarship and educational programmes.”
Photos of the staffer working on the plan—in full view of fellow passengers on public transit—had been published by ProPublica the previous day (23 November). Formatted as a 25-item to-do list, the draft focused largely on the beleaguered National Museum of American History (NMAH), a recent focal point in the White House’s attempts to rewrite US history.
The list included firing NMAH’s director and a dozen other administrators and curators, opening a new permanent exhibition centred on “Western civilisation inheritance”, erecting a new “colossus statue” of George Washington for NMAH’s entrance and overhauling its online curriculum for schoolchildren to “realign educational materials with patriotism, not ideology”. The plan also called for a review of Smithsonian grants to “woke third parties” like the American Alliance of Museums.
Given that it was in process prior to the midterm elections—which resulted in a landslide for Democrats, who gained a majority in both houses of congress—it remains unclear if this plan for the Smithsonian is still in the works. However, congressional Democrats are ready to fight.
“I intend to investigate these matters in the 120th congress and vigorously defend the Smithsonian’s independence,” Chellie Pingree, the ranking member of the congressional subcommittee that funds the Smithsonian, wrote in a letter to the institution’s Board of Regents after the ProPublica leak. “This reporting is extremely concerning, but not surprising given this administration’s previous attempts to illegally impound Smithsonian Institution-appropriated funding, use federal agencies to spread misinformation about the Smithsonian, and release a demonstrably false report accusing the Smithsonian Institution of systemic bias in its curatorial decisions.”
US President Donald Trump has been steadily attacking the Smithsonian ever since he took office for his second term, with a goal of realigning the institution to complement his own political agenda. Last year, Trump attempted to fire the director of the National Portrait Gallery, Kim Sajet, over her support for diversity, equity and inclusion programmes. She later resigned and now heads the Milwaukee Art Museum in Wisconsin.
In July, NMAH director Anthea M. Hartig was summoned to appear before congress and interrogated by Republican lawmakers after a White House report concluded the museum was not “proudly patriotic” with leadership having “denigrated and displaced whites, males, Christians and Americans”. A few days later, Trump ordered that signs be placed outside the NMAH, warning visitors of "ideological capture" and "inaccurate information" inside. (The signs have yet to be erected.)

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/.title: Christie’s Adds UK Auction House Dreweatts to Its Portfolio
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/.author: Hikmat Mohammed
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/.text:
Christie’s has added the UK auction house Dreweatts to its portfolio.
In a statement on Wednesday, Christie’s chief executive Bonnie Brennan said that the auction house has long admired Dreweatts. “Most importantly, our clients collect across categories and at every price point, and together we have the opportunity to provide them with an even broader and more complete level of service. Both businesses will continue to operate much as they do today, while building on their respective strengths and the significant opportunities we see for future growth,” she said.
Dreweatts specializes in single-owner collections and country house sales, ranging from furniture and works of art, old masters, modern and contemporary art, Asian and European ceramics, modern design, jewelry, silver, luxury accessories, clocks and wine. The auction house was founded in 1759 by Thomas Davis, a cabinetmaker, upholsterer and land agent from Abingdon, Oxfordshire. Dreweatts operates its main salesroom from its country house, Donnington Priory, in Newbury, Berkshire, and also has a showroom in London on Pall Mall.
Henry House, chief executive of Dreweatts, said in a statement that under this new arrangement “we can use the additional advantage of one another’s expertise to better serve our buyers and sellers. Dreweatts has had a parent company before, which enabled us to grow the business and prosper, and this move is an extension of that model.” He added that the Christie’s acquisition provides certainty for the auction house and that Dreweatts will continue, under his and chairman Will Richards’ stewardship.
Christie’s president of EMEA, Anthea Peers, said that the François Pinault-owned auction house recognized Dreweatts as a “healthy, compatible business to our own and the value it can add to what we do for all of our clients.”
On November 19, Dreweatts presented its Fine Watches & Luxury Accessories auction that totaled £529,934 with an 89% sell-through rate. The sale included fine watches, designer handbags, writing instruments and luxury objects from Patek Philippe, Cartier, Hermès, Chanel and Montblanc. The top lots were a Lange & Söhne that sold for £49,780 and a Montblanc black porcelain fountain pen that sold for £8,320.

https://taz.de/Pflegereform-und-Betroffe.title: Pflegereform und Betroffene: „Dieses Gesetz muss gestoppt werden“
https://taz.de/Pflegereform-und-Betroffe.author: Barbara Dribbusch
https://taz.de/Pflegereform-und-Betroffe.text:
Pflegereform und Betroffene: „Dieses Gesetz muss gestoppt werden“
In einer Anhörung im Bundestag kritisieren Angehörige und Pflegedienste das neue Pflegespargesetz, das schon in sechs Wochen in Kraft treten soll
Es ist schon eine Form von politischem Wahnsinn: Da ist ein Gesetz geplant, das für Hundertausende von Pflegebedürftigen und ihre Angehörigen bedeutet, dass ab 1.Januar kein Pflegedienst mehr vorbeikommt, weil es nicht mehr bezahlt wird. Und bei der Anhörung am Mittwoch im Bundestag hatte man den Eindruck, dass die Betroffenen doch noch irgendwie hoffen, dass es so schlimm nicht kommt. Dass das Gesetz jedenfalls nicht in der bisherigen Form verabschiedet wird und daher auch nicht am 1.Januar, also in sechs Wochen, in Kraft treten kann.
„Eine Riesenkatastrophe ist dieses Gesetz“, sagte Wiebke Worm vom Verein Pflegende Angehörige bei der Anhörung. „Dieses Gesetz muss gestoppt werden. Wir brauchen einen Neustart“.
Mit dem geplanten Spargesetz sollen der hochdefizitären Pflegekasse Milliarden an Euro eingespart werden. So soll es nicht mehr wie bisher möglich sein, dass Hilfskräfte stunden- oder tageweise als Ersatzpflege in den Haushalten einspringen und Angehörige damit entlasten. Diese können bisher dafür bis zu 3.450 Euro im Jahr relativ unbürokratisch mit der Pflegekasse abrechnen. Der Posten dieser sogenannten „Verhinderungspflege“ wird im sogenannten Pflegeneuordnungsgesetz (PNOG) gestrichen. Zwar werden im Gegenzug andere Budgets für die Pflegehaushalte erhöht. „Es bleibt aber eine finanzielle Lücke“ sagte Elisabeth Fix vom Deutschen Caritasverband.
Fix rügte, dass zudem mit dem neuen Gesetz professionelle Pflegedienste keine Dienstleistungen im Haushalt mehr erbringen und abrechnen dürfen. Dies soll künftig nur noch Alltagshelfer:innen vorbehalten sein, die nach den entsprechenden Gesetzen der Länder zertifiziert sein müssen. In vielen Regionen seien die Pflegedienste aber die einzigen, die solche Alltagshilfen leisteten, sagte Fix. „Dann müssen die Pflegedienste diesen Haushalten sagen, dass sie ab Januar nicht mehr kommen“.
Gerügt wurde auch der Wegfall des sogenannten Entlastungsbetrags im niedrigsten Pflegegrad 1. Das sind 131 Euro im Monat, die zur Finanzierung von Alltagshilfen oder Begleitungen eingesetzt werden können. Lilja Helms von der Deutschen Alzheimerinitiative sagte, für viele Demenzkranke auch im niedrigen Pflegegrad 1 seien diesen Hilfen, die ja auch einen regelmäßigen Besuch der Helfer:innen garantieren, wichtig, „viele Menschen mit Demenz leben allein“.
Das Gesetz soll am 11.Dezember in zweiter und dritter Lesung im Bundestag verabschiedet werden. Nach Proteststürmen und Petitionen von Angehörigenverbänden und Sozialverbänden hatte Bundesgesundheitsminister Carsten Linnemann (CDU) bei der ersten Lesung vor drei Wochen schon angekündigt, den Gesetzentwurf noch einmal in Teilen „nachzubessern“. Übergangsfristen für die neuen Regelungen sind im Gespräch und auch Modifizierungen in der Streichung der Verhinderungspflege, hieß es in Koalitionskreisen.
Linnemann hatte aber auch auf das Defizit in der Pflegeversicherung hingewiesen, das ohne die Reformen im kommenden Jahr schon knapp 8 Milliarden Euro betragen würde.
Die SPD-Fraktion möchte, dass die privaten Pflegekassen (PPK) zu einem Risikostrukturausgleich mit den gesetzlichen Kassen, der sogenannten sozialen Pflegeversicherung (SPV) herangezogen werden. Dies soll die Finanzprobleme der gesetzlichen Pflegeversicherung lösen helfen. Frauke Fiegl, Co-Vorsitzende des Verbandes der privaten Krankenversicherung (PKV) erklärte während der Anhörung, diese würde für die Versicherten in den gesetzlichen Pflegekassen „nicht viel bringen“, sondern nur zu einer monatlichen Beitragsentlastung von 70 Cent führen.

https://www.humanite.fr/politique/fabien.title: Au Congrès des maires, Fabien Roussel défend les communes dans la bataille présidentielle
https://www.humanite.fr/politique/fabien.author: Lisa Guillemin
https://www.humanite.fr/politique/fabien.text:
Écoles menacées, services publics éloignés, investissements fragilisés : les maires communistes ont exposé leurs difficultés au candidat du PCF, mercredi 25 novembre. De leur réunion aux allées du salon, il défend les moyens d’une « gauche qui protège ».
Le programme est chargé, mais Fabien Roussel a son « obsession » : défendre les communes. Mercredi 25 novembre, le maire de Saint-Amand-les-Eaux vient écouter ses homologues communistes au congrès de l’Association des maires de France (AMF) : « quand on est maire, on sait l’importance d’une commune dans la vie des citoyens. C’est le cœur de la République »
La matinée commence par un entretien à huis clos avec Philippe Laurent, maire UDI de Sceaux et concurrent de David Lisnard à la présidence de l’AMF. Le secrétaire national du PCF l’a assuré de son soutien, ainsi que de celui de ses homologues communistes, face à l’ultralibéral cannois. Prôner la réduction...
